
Munnadi phases-la nee paartha pattern than kavanikanum:

| JS/TS      | Python            |
| ---------- | ----------------- |
| `function` | `def`             |
| `{ }`      | `:` + indentation |
| `;`        | thevai illa       |

## Function-a call pannradhu [#function-a-call-pannradhu]

JS maadhiri exact-a same:

```python
result = add(2, 3)
print(result)   # 5
```

## Parameters [#parameters]

Mேlе irukura `a` mattrum `b` **parameters** — function call pannum bothu adhu expect pannura
values. Python-la type declare pannanum-nu thevai illa (adha type hints vechi next-la
paapom), edhu value pass pannalum adha use pannikkum.

## return [#return]

`return`, JS maadhiri than exact-a work aagum — caller-ku oru value return pannitu, function-a
udane exit pannidum.

```python
def is_adult(age):
    if age >= 18:
        return True
    return False

print(is_adult(20))   # True
```

Python function-la `return` statement illana, adhu `None` return pannum — JS-la `return`
illatha function `undefined` return panradhu maadhiri than idea.

```python
def greet(name):
    print(f"Hello {name}")

result = greet("John")
print(result)   # None
```


# Phase 3 — Functions (/tanglish/docs/phase-3)



Estimated time: **\~1 hour**.

## Goals [#goals]

Indha phase mudichadhukku apparam, intha topics ellam unakku comfortable ah irukanum:

* parameters
* `return`
* default parameters
* keyword arguments
* type hints
* `*args`
* `**kwargs` basics

Type hints indha phase-la romba important — **FastAPI idha read pannum** requests-a validate
pannradhukku mattrum docs automatic-a generate pannradhukku, so ippove idha comfortable ah
kathukittaa apparam romba use aagum.

Ovvoru topic-um sidebar-la thani page ah irukku. Ella page-layum JS/TS → Python compare
panni explain pannirukom, adha followed by oru chinna example.

## Cheat sheet [#cheat-sheet]

```text
JavaScript / TypeScript                       Python
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
function add(a, b) {                          def add(a, b):
  return a + b;                                   return a + b
}

function add(a = 1) { }                        def add(a=1):

function add(...rest) { }                      def add(*args):

function add({ ...obj }) { }                   def add(**kwargs):

function add(a: number, b: number): number {   def add(a: int, b: int) -> int:
  return a + b;                                    return a + b
}
```


# Type Hints (/tanglish/docs/phase-3/type-hints)



Function work aana apparam, adha **type hints** vechi annotate pannalaam — ovvoru
parameter-um return value-um enna type-nu describe pannum.

```python
def add(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return a + b
```

* `a: int` mattrum `b: int` — ovvoru parameter-oda expected type
* `-> int` — return type

Idhu TypeScript-la irundhu varra unakku romba familiar ah irukum:

```ts
function add(a: number, b: number): number {
  return a + b;
}
```

## TypeScript-la irundhu important difference [#typescript-la-irundhu-important-difference]

TypeScript oda types **compile time**-la check pannappadum — andha rules violate pannura
code-a compiler build panna refuse pannidum. Python oda type hints, language-e enforce
pannadhu:

```python
def add(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return a + b

add("2", "3")   # correct-a run aagum, "23" return pannum — Python hints-a check pannadhu
```

Idhu crash aagadhu — Python code-a eppadi eluthiruko adha appadiye run pannum. Andha hints,
adha padikura tools-ku matum than matter aagum.

## FastAPI ku yen important [#fastapi-ku-yen-important]

Idhu than periya point: **FastAPI unga type hints-a runtime-la read pannum** mattrum adha
vechi incoming requests-a validate pannum, data-va automatic-a convert pannum, interactive
API docs generate pannum — nee extra validation code onnume eluthama. So plain Python type
hints-a ignore pannalum, nee poga poravu frameworks adha definitely ignore pannadhu.

## Nee use pannura common types [#nee-use-pannura-common-types]

```python
def example(
    name: str,
    age: int,
    price: float,
    is_active: bool,
    tags: list,
    metadata: dict,
) -> None:
    pass
```

## Optional values [#optional-values]

Oru value `None` aaga vaaippu irundha, adha explicit-a mark pannu:

```python
def greet(name: str | None = None):
    if name is None:
        print("Hello stranger")
    else:
        print(f"Hello {name}")
```

`str | None` na "oru string, illana `None`"-nu padikalam — TypeScript oda `string | null`
maadhiri than idea.


# class & object (/tanglish/docs/phase-4/classes-and-objects)



## class [#class]

Class na objects create pannradhukku oru blueprint. Keyword nee already ariyum vaarthai than:

TypeScript:

```ts
class User {
}
```

Python:

```python
class User:
    pass
```

Functions maadhiri than same pattern — `{ }` ku badhila `:` + indentation. `pass` na "ippodikku
empty body" nu artham (idha Phase 1-lame paartha).

## object [#object]

**object** (Python idha **instance** nu solum) na class-la irundhu create pannina oru real
value.

TypeScript:

```ts
const user = new User();
```

Python:

```python
user = User()
```

Unlearn pannanum-na oru thing: **Python-la `new` keyword edhuvum kidayathu**. Class name-a
function maadhiri call panna, object create aagidum.


# Phase 4 — Python OOP (/tanglish/docs/phase-4)



Estimated time: **\~1.5 hours**.

Idhula deep-a poga vendam — simple classes padikkaradhukku, eluthuradhukku podhuma irundha
OOP than venum. Unakku TypeScript theriyum-nu bothu idhu easy-a irukum, Python classes almost
same maadhiri than work aagum.

## Goals [#goals]

Indha phase mudichadhukku apparam, intha topics ellam unakku puriyanum:

* `class`
* object
* `__init__`
* `self`
* instance variables
* methods
* inheritance
* `super()`

Ovvoru topic-um sidebar-la thani page ah irukku. Ella page-layum TypeScript → Python compare
panni explain pannirukom, adha followed by oru chinna example.

## Cheat sheet [#cheat-sheet]

```text
TypeScript                             Python
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
class User {                           class User:
  name: string;

  constructor(name: string) {              def __init__(self, name):
    this.name = name;                          self.name = name
  }

  greet(): string {                        def greet(self):
    return `Hello ${this.name}`;              return f"Hello {self.name}"
  }
}

new User("John")                       User("John")

this.name                              self.name

class Dog extends Animal {             class Dog(Animal):
  constructor(name: string) {              def __init__(self, name):
    super(name);                               super().__init__(name)
  }
}
```


# Inheritance & super() (/tanglish/docs/phase-4/inheritance)



## Inheritance [#inheritance]

TypeScript oda `extends`, Python-la class name-ku apparam **parentheses** aaga maarum.

TypeScript:

```ts
class Animal {
  name: string;

  constructor(name: string) {
    this.name = name;
  }

  speak(): string {
    return `${this.name} makes a sound`;
  }
}

class Dog extends Animal {
  speak(): string {
    return `${this.name} barks`;
  }
}
```

Python:

```python
class Animal:
    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name

    def speak(self):
        return f"{self.name} makes a sound"

class Dog(Animal):
    def speak(self):
        return f"{self.name} barks"

dog = Dog("Rex")
print(dog.speak())   # Rex barks
```

`Dog`, `Animal`-la irundhu ellathayum inherit pannikkum — `__init__`-um sagitham — `speak()`
matum override pannum.

## super() [#super]

Child class-ku thani `__init__` venum, aana parent oda setup logic-um run aaganum-nu bothu,
`super()` call pannu — TypeScript-oda constructor-kulla `super(...)` panra same idea than.

TypeScript:

```ts
class Dog extends Animal {
  breed: string;

  constructor(name: string, breed: string) {
    super(name);
    this.breed = breed;
  }
}
```

Python:

```python
class Dog(Animal):
    def __init__(self, name, breed):
        super().__init__(name)
        self.breed = breed
```

Difference: TypeScript direct-a `super(name)` call pannum; Python first `super()` call
pannum (arguments edhuvum illama) parent-oda reference edukkum, apparam adhoda mela
`.__init__(name)` call pannum. Result same than — `Dog` edhavadhu add pannradhukku munnadi
parent oda constructor run aagi `self.name`-a set pannidum.


# __init__ & self (/tanglish/docs/phase-4/init-and-self)



## **init** — constructor [#init--constructor]

`__init__` na Python oda constructor — nee object create pannum bothu idhu automatic-a run
aagum, TypeScript oda `constructor` maadhiri than.

TypeScript:

```ts
class User {
  name: string;
  age: number;

  constructor(name: string, age: number) {
    this.name = name;
    this.age = age;
  }
}

const user = new User('John', 25);
```

Python:

```python
class User:
    def __init__(self, name, age):
        self.name = name
        self.age = age

user = User("John", 25)
```

## self — Python oda this [#self--python-oda-this]

`self`, current object-a refer pannum, TypeScript-la `this&#x60; panra same job than. Key
difference: **`self`-a ovvoru method-oda first parameter-a explicit-a eluthanum** — JS/TS
maadhiri `this`-a Python automatic-a invisible-a add pannadhu.

```python
def __init__(self, name, age):
    self.name = name   # self.<edhuvum> = oru instance variable
    self.age = age
```

## Instance variables [#instance-variables]

`self.name` mattrum `self.age` **instance variables** — andha specific object-ku matum
sonthamana data, TS class-la `this.name` maadhiri exact-a. Nee create pannura ovvoru
object-um adhoda own copy-a vechikkum:

```python
john = User("John", 25)
david = User("David", 30)

print(john.name)    # John
print(david.name)   # David
```


# Methods (/tanglish/docs/phase-4/methods)



**Method** na class-kulla define pannina oru function than. `__init__`-um technically oru
method than — create aagum bothu run aagura oru special method matum than.

TypeScript:

```ts
class User {
  name: string;

  constructor(name: string) {
    this.name = name;
  }

  greet(): string {
    return `Hello ${this.name}`;
  }
}

const user = new User('John');
console.log(user.greet());
```

Python:

```python
class User:
    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name

    def greet(self):
        return f"Hello {self.name}"

user = User("John")
print(user.greet())
```

## self innum varudhu [#self-innum-varudhu]

Ovvoru method-um `self`-a adhoda first parameter-a venum, object oda instance variables
(indha `self.name`) read pannradhukku. Idhu munnadi page-la paartha same `self` than —
Python matum idha ovvoru method signature-layum explicit-a name pannanum-nu solum.

**Aana method-a call pannum bothu, `self`-a nee pass panna vendam** — `user.greet()`,
`user.greet(user)` illa. Dot-ku munnadi irukura object-a vechi Python `self`-a automatic-a
fill pannikkum; nee **remaining** parameters-a matum than pass pannanum.


# Dictionary Comprehension (/tanglish/docs/phase-5/dictionary-comprehension)



List comprehension panra same idea than, aana idhu oru `dict`-a build pannum — oru single
expression-ku badhila ovvoru side-layum `key: value` pair irukum.

```python
squares = {
    x: x * x
    for x in range(5)
}

print(squares)   # {0: 0, 1: 1, 2: 4, 3: 9, 4: 16}
```

```text
{key: value for item in iterable}
```

JS-la idha maadhiri clean-a direct equivalent kidayathu — usually `[key, value]` pairs oda
oru array build pannitu, `Object.fromEntries()` vechi convert pannanum:

```js
const squares = Object.fromEntries(
  Array.from({ length: 5 }, (_, x) => [x, x * x]),
);
```

Idhu Python, JS/TS-a vida noticeably ergonomic-a irukura cases-la onnu. List comprehension
maadhiri idhu-um same `if` filter support pannum:

```python
even_squares = {x: x * x for x in range(10) if x % 2 == 0}
# {0: 0, 2: 4, 4: 16, 6: 36, 8: 64}
```


# enumerate (/tanglish/docs/phase-5/enumerate)



`enumerate()`, oru iterable-a wrap pannum, so ovvoru loop turn-um unakku **index**-um
**value**-um rendaiyum kudukkum.

```python
users = ["John", "David"]

for index, user in enumerate(users):
    print(index, user)
```

```text
0 John
1 David
```

JS-la idhe result-a edukka rendu ways irukku:

```js
const users = ['John', 'David'];

users.forEach((user, index) => {
  console.log(index, user);
});

// or, real `for` loop venum-na:
for (const [index, user] of users.entries()) {
  console.log(index, user);
}
```

`arr.entries()` than close-a match aagum — idhu-um `[index, value]` pairs kudukkum, Python
oda `enumerate()` maadhiri same shape than.

## Vera number-la irundhu start pannradhu [#vera-number-la-irundhu-start-pannradhu]

`0`-la count start panna vendam-na `start` pass pannu:

```python
for index, user in enumerate(users, start=1):
    print(index, user)
```

```text
1 John
2 David
```


# Phase 5 — Python-specific Features (/tanglish/docs/phase-5)



Estimated time: **\~1.5 hours**.

Idhukku clean-a JS/TS equivalent kidayathu, aana real Python code-la idha nee constant-a
paapa. Hours spend panni perfect panna vendam — goal na idha **comfortable-a read** pannradhu
matum than.

## Goals [#goals]

Indha phase mudichadhukku apparam, intha topics ellam nee comfortable-a read pannanum:

* list comprehension
* dictionary comprehension
* `enumerate`
* `zip`

Ovvoru topic-um sidebar-la thani page ah irukku. Ella page-layum JS/TS → Python compare
panni explain pannirukom, adha followed by oru chinna example.

## Cheat sheet [#cheat-sheet]

```text
JavaScript / TypeScript                        Python
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
arr.map(x => x * x)                            [x * x for x in arr]

arr.filter(x => x % 2 === 0)                   [x for x in arr if x % 2 == 0]
   .map(x => x * x)                                x * x

Object.fromEntries(                            {x: x * x for x in range(5)}
  Array.from({ length: 5 },
    (_, x) => [x, x * x])
)

arr.forEach((v, i) => { ... })                 for i, v in enumerate(arr):
for (const [i, v] of arr.entries())

manual index loop /                            for a, b in zip(arr1, arr2):
lodash zip(arr1, arr2)
```


# List Comprehension (/tanglish/docs/phase-5/list-comprehension)



List comprehension, irukura oru iterable-la irundhu oru new list-a, single line-la build
pannum.

JavaScript:

```js
const numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5];
const squares = numbers.map((x) => x * x);
```

Python:

```python
numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

squares = [x * x for x in numbers]
```

Idha ippadi padi: &#x2A;*"`numbers`-la irukura ovvoru `x`-kum, `x * x`"**. General shape idhu than:

```text
[expression for item in iterable]
```

`.map()` panra same idea than, callback-ku badhila oru expression-a matum eluthuvom.

## Condition-oda [#condition-oda]

End-la `if` podu, JS-la `.filter().map()` rendu steps-la pannuradha, oru step-la pannalam:

```js
const evenSquares = numbers.filter((x) => x % 2 === 0).map((x) => x * x);
```

```python
even_squares = [x * x for x in numbers if x % 2 == 0]
```

```text
[expression for item in iterable if condition]
```

Real Python code padikka start pannina apparam, idha nee constant-a paapa — first time
paakumbothu weird-a irukum, aana idhu oru list-a build pannura compact `for` loop matum
than.


# zip (/tanglish/docs/phase-5/zip)



`zip()`, rendu (allathu adhukku mela) lists-la irundhu items-a position vechi pair pannum,
so nee adha onnaaga loop pannalam.

```python
names = ["John", "David"]
ages = [25, 30]

for name, age in zip(names, ages):
    print(name, age)
```

```text
John 25
David 30
```

JS/TS-la direct-a built-in equivalent kidayathu — usually index vechi loop pannuvom:

```js
const names = ['John', 'David'];
const ages = [25, 30];

for (let i = 0; i < names.length; i++) {
  console.log(names[i], ages[i]);
}
```

`zip()` direct-a padikka easy ("indha rendu lists-a onnaaga loop pannu") — index-a manual-a
manage panna vendam.

## Lengths match aagatha bothu [#lengths-match-aagatha-bothu]

Lists same length illana, `zip()` **chinna** list mudinja stop aagidum — error edhuvum
throw pannadhu:

```python
names = ["John", "David", "Sam"]
ages = [25, 30]

list(zip(names, ages))
# [("John", 25), ("David", 30)]  — "Sam" quietly drop aagidum
```


# Phase 6 — Exceptions + Modules (/tanglish/docs/phase-6)



Estimated time: **\~1 hour**.

## Goals [#goals]

Indha phase mudichadhukku apparam, intha topics ellam unakku puriyanum:

* `try` / `except`
* `raise`
* modules — `import`, `from ... import ...`
* files mattrum modules eppadi related aagirukku-nu

Ovvoru topic-um sidebar-la thani page ah irukku. Ella page-layum JS/TS → Python compare
panni explain pannirukom, adha followed by oru chinna example.

## Cheat sheet [#cheat-sheet]

```text
JavaScript / TypeScript                     Python
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
try {                                       try:
  doSomethingRisky();                           result = 10 / 0
} catch (error) {                           except ZeroDivisionError:
  console.log(error.message);                  print("Cannot divide by zero")
}

throw new Error("Invalid value")            raise ValueError("Invalid value")

// users.js                                 # users.py
export function getUser() { }               def get_user():
                                                 ...

// main.js                                  # main.py
import { getUser } from './users.js';       from users import get_user

import * as fs from 'fs';                   import json
fs.readFileSync(...)                         json.dumps(...)
```


# Modules & Imports (/tanglish/docs/phase-6/modules-and-imports)



## Ovvoru file-um oru module [#ovvoru-file-um-oru-module]

JS/TS-la, oru file edhavadhu share pannanum-na explicit-a `export` pannanum:

```js
// users.js
export function getUser() {
  // ...
}
```

```js
// main.js
import { getUser } from './users.js';
```

Python-la, **ovvoru `.py` file-um automatic-a oru module** — top level-la define
pannirukura edhuvum (functions, classes, variables) vera file import panniikalam, `export`
keyword edhuvum illama:

```python
# users.py
def get_user():
    ...
```

```python
# main.py
from users import get_user
```

Module oda name na, filename-la irundhu `.py` remove pannitta than — `users.py` na module
`users` aagum.

## Import panna rendu ways [#import-panna-rendu-ways]

**Specific name import pannradhu** — direct-a use pannu, prefix edhuvum illa:

```python
from users import get_user

get_user()
```

**Whole module import pannradhu** — adhoda name vechi ellathayum access pannu:

```python
import json

json.dumps({"name": "John"})
```

Idhu rendaavadhu style, JS oda namespace import maadhiri than:

```js
import * as fs from 'fs';

fs.readFileSync('file.txt');
```

Indha `json`, Python oda **built-in modules**-la onnu — Python-oda vandhe irukum, install
pannanum-nu thevai illa (Node oda built-in `fs` allathu `path` maadhiri than).

## Convention vazhi "private" — enforce pannadhu [#convention-vazhi-private--enforce-pannadhu]

Underscore-la start aagura oru name (`_helper`), idhu internal, vera edho import pannak
koodadhu-nu oru signal — aana Phase 1-la paartha `MAX_USERS` constant convention maadhiri
than, Python idha import panna actual-a stop pannadhu. Idhu vera developers rely aagura oru
convention than, hard rule illa.


# raise (/tanglish/docs/phase-6/raise)



`raise` na Python oda `throw` — idhu current code-a stop pannitu, close-la irukura matching
`except`-ku control-a kudukkum.

JavaScript:

```js
throw new Error('Invalid value');
```

Python:

```python
raise ValueError("Invalid value")
```

## Oru generic Error ku badhila built-in exception types [#oru-generic-error-ku-badhila-built-in-exception-types]

JS mostly oru `Error` class than kudukkum, adhoda message allathu oru custom subclass vechi
nee errors-a distinguish pannuva. Python-la, common situations ku several **built-in
exception types** irukku, nee match aagura onnu pick pannikanum:

```python
raise ValueError("age must be positive")
raise TypeError("expected a string")
raise KeyError("user_id")
```

Idhu than munnadi page specific exception types-a catch pannu-nu solradhukku exact reason —
`raise` mattrum `except` rendu side-layum same names than.

## Nee raise pannadha catch pannradhu [#nee-raise-pannadha-catch-pannradhu]

```python
def set_age(age):
    if age < 0:
        raise ValueError("age must be positive")
    return age

try:
    set_age(-5)
except ValueError as e:
    print(e)   # age must be positive
```

JS-um same pattern than:

```js
function setAge(age) {
  if (age < 0) {
    throw new Error('age must be positive');
  }
  return age;
}

try {
  setAge(-5);
} catch (error) {
  console.log(error.message); // age must be positive
}
```


# try / except (/tanglish/docs/phase-6/try-except)



## Basic shape [#basic-shape]

JavaScript:

```js
try {
  doSomethingRisky();
} catch (error) {
  console.log('Something went wrong');
}
```

Python:

```python
try:
    result = 10 / 0
except ZeroDivisionError:
    print("Cannot divide by zero")
```

`except` na Python oda `catch`. Baaki ellam same than padikkalam: fail aaga vaaippu irukura
code first block-la, recovery logic second block-la irukum.

**JS-la irundhu varra oru gotcha:** JavaScript-la `10 / 0` throw pannadhu — quietly
`Infinity` kudukkum. Python-la, zero-la divide pannina **exception raise aagum**. Different
languages-ku, error-nu enna count aagum-nu different rules.

## Everything-a illa, specific errors-a matum catch pannu [#everything-a-illa-specific-errors-a-matum-catch-pannu]

JS oda `catch (error)`, edhuvum question kekama catch pannidum. Python, mele example-la
irukura `ZeroDivisionError` maadhiri, nee expect pannura **specific exception type**-a name
panna encourage pannum. Nee frequent-a paakura built-in ones:

```text
ZeroDivisionError   zero-la divide pannradhu
ValueError          value-oda type correct-a irukku, aana bad value (example: int("abc"))
KeyError            dict-la oru key illa
IndexError           list index range-a mīra irukku
TypeError            operation-ku wrong type kudutha
```

`except Exception` vechi broad-a-um catch pannalaam, `str(e)` vechi message-a read
pannalaam — JS-la `error.message` read panradhu maadhiri than:

```python
try:
    result = 10 / 0
except Exception as e:
    print(str(e))   # "division by zero"
```

Enna guard pannuroam-nu theriyum bothu, specific exception-a name pannradha prefer pannu —
idhu than idiomatic Python style, adhoda mela, unrelated bug-a accidental-a swallow
pannradha idhu stop pannum.

## finally [#finally]

JS maadhiri than, `finally` eppovum run aagum, exception aaganalum aagalanalum:

```python
try:
    result = 10 / 0
except ZeroDivisionError:
    print("Cannot divide by zero")
finally:
    print("Done trying")
```


# Container Hints (/tanglish/docs/phase-7/container-hints)



Idhu varaikkum type hints oru single value-a describe pannirukku. Containers-ku oru extra
piece of information venum: **adhukulla enna irukku**.

## list\[...] [#list]

TypeScript:

```ts
let users: string[] = ['John', 'David'];
// or: Array<string>
```

Python:

```python
users: list[str] = ["John", "David"]
```

`list[str]` na "oru list, strings oda"-nu padikanum — brackets-kulla irukura type, list-la
irukura ovvoru item-a-um describe pannum.

## dict\[...] [#dict]

TypeScript-la close-a irukura match `Record<KeyType, ValueType>`:

```ts
const users: Record<number, string> = {
  1: 'John',
  2: 'David',
};
```

Python:

```python
users: dict[int, str] = {1: "John", 2: "David"}
```

General shape `dict[KeyType, ValueType]` than — key type first, value type second, andha
order-la.

```text
list[ItemType]
dict[KeyType, ValueType]
```

Indha reading habit-a vechiko — next page-la nested types build up pannradhukku same
pattern-a than use pannuvom.


# Phase 7 — Type Hints (/tanglish/docs/phase-7)



Estimated time: **\~1 hour**. ⭐⭐⭐

Idhula real-a time spend pannu — naalaikku irundhu, nee touch pannura almost ella function
mattrum data model-layum type hints paapa, especially FastAPI-la.

Phase 3-lame type hints-a function parameters mattrum return values-la introduce pannirukom.
Indha phase adha wider-a extend pannum: plain variables-a annotate pannradhu, mattrum
list, dict maadhiri containers oda **shape**-a describe pannradhu — "idhu oru list"-nu matum
illa, "yenna list"-nu.

## Goals [#goals]

Indha phase mudichadhukku apparam, intha type hints-a nee comfortable-a padikkanum,
eluthanum:

```python
name: str
age: int
price: float
active: bool
```

```python
def get_user(user_id: int) -> dict:
    ...
```

```python
users: list[str]
```

```python
users: dict[int, str]
```

```python
name: str | None = None
```

```python
users: list[dict[str, str]]
```

Idhu ku mela edhuvum worry panna vendam ippodikku — generics, `Protocol`, `Callable`
maadhiri things, unakku actual-a thevai padra bothu kathukalam.

## Cheat sheet [#cheat-sheet]

```text
TypeScript                                   Python
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
let name: string                             name: str
let age: number                              age: int
let price: number                            price: float
let active: boolean                          active: bool

function getUser(id: number): object         def get_user(user_id: int) -> dict:

string[]  /  Array<string>                    list[str]
Record<number, string>                        dict[int, str]

string | null                                 str | None

Array<Record<string, string>>                 list[dict[str, str]]
```


# Optional & Nested Types (/tanglish/docs/phase-7/optional-and-nested)



## Optional — None aaga vaaippu irukura value [#optional--none-aaga-vaaippu-irukura-value]

Idha Phase 3-lame chinna-a paartha. `| None` oru value-a optional-nu mark pannum:

```python
name: str | None = None
```

TypeScript:

```ts
let name: string | null = null;
```

`str | None`-a "oru string, illana `None`"-nu padi — TypeScript-oda `string | null` maadhiri
than same union-type idea, Python-oda sonthamana "value edhuvum illa" (Phase 1) matum
`null`-ku badhila irukku.

Idhu, "value edhuvum kudukkalana" nu oru sensible default irukura function parameters-la
constant-a varum:

```python
def get_user(user_id: int, name: str | None = None) -> dict:
    ...
```

## Nested types [#nested-types]

Container hints-a serthu combine pannalam — dicts oda list, lists oda dict, appadi. Idha
**inside-out** padi: first innermost type-a find pannu, apparam outward-a wrap pannu.

```python
users: list[dict[str, str]]
```

Inside-out padikkalam:

1. `dict[str, str]` — keys mattrum values rendum strings-a irukura oru dict
2. `list[...]` — andha dicts oda oru list

So whole thing oda artham: &#x2A;*"oru list, adhula ovvoru item-um string-to-string dict."**

TypeScript:

```ts
let users: Array<Record<string, string>>;
```

Idha exact shape-a nee constant-a paapa — "pala records"-a most APIs represent pannradhu
idhu than, oru list of dicts, ovvoru record-um oru dict (Phase 2-oda nested-data example,
ippo hints-oda).

## Ippodikku idhu podhum [#ippodikku-idhu-podhum]

`str | None`, `list[...]`, mattrum `dict[...]` — nee daily eluthura vast majority of type
hints-a cover pannidum. Generics, `Protocol`, allathu `Callable` types maadhiri things,
adha unakku actual-a thevai padra case hit aana apparam kathukalam — adhukku munnadi illa.


# Variable & Function Hints (/tanglish/docs/phase-7/variable-and-function-hints)



## Variable type hints [#variable-type-hints]

TypeScript:

```ts
let name: string = 'John';
let age: number = 25;
let price: number = 99.99;
let active: boolean = true;
```

Python:

```python
name: str = "John"
age: int = 25
price: float = 99.99
active: bool = True
```

TypeScript maadhiri than same idea — `name: type`. Indha exact naalu types Phase 1-la
annotation illama nee paartha; ippo adha explicit-a label pannuroam matum than.

Value edhuvum kudukkama-um oru variable-a annotate pannalam — idhu class bodies (Phase 4)
mattrum data models maadhiri idangala-la common, andha idangala-la nee oru shape-a describe
pannuroam, udane edhavadhu assign pannama:

```python
name: str
age: int
```

## Function hints — oru recap [#function-hints--oru-recap]

Phase 3-lame idha cover pannirukom, so idhu shape-a ninaivupaduthara matum than, ippo nee
plain-variable version-um paartha apparam:

```python
def get_user(user_id: int) -> dict:
    ...
```

```ts
function getUser(userId: number): object {
  // ...
}
```

`user_id: int` na oru parameter hint (variable hint maadhiri than), `-> dict` na return
type — TypeScript-la `:` apparam varra return type maadhiri exact-a.

Phase 3-la irundhu oru reminder: idhu ellam Python-e enforce pannadhu. Nee build pannura
frameworks than — especially FastAPI — indha hints-a actual-a read panni act pannum.


# def, async def & await (/tanglish/docs/phase-8/async-and-await)



## def vs. async def [#def-vs-async-def]

Oru normal function synchronously than run aagum, start-la irundhu end varaikkum, exact-a
oru normal JS function maadhiri than:

```python
def get_user():
    ...
```

`def`-ku munnadi `async` podradhu, adha oru **asynchronous function**-a maathum — pause
pannitu resume pannalam, wait pannum bothu program-oda remaining part-a block pannama:

```python
async def get_user():
    ...
```

```js
async function getUser() {
  // ...
}
```

Same keyword than, same idea than, `function`-ku munnadi ku badhila `def`-ku munnadi than
podrom.

## await [#await]

`async def` function-kulla, `await` andha line-la pause pannum, nee await pannradhu edhu
mudiyum varaikkum — apparam adhoda result-oda resume pannum. Idhu JS-oda exact same mental
model than:

```python
async def get_user():
    data = await fetch_data()
    return data
```

```js
async function getUser() {
  const data = await fetchData();
  return data;
}
```

JS maadhiri than, `await`, `async def` function-**kulla** matum than use pannalam — regular
function-la illa.

## JS-la irundhu oru real difference: async function-a call pannradhu [#js-la-irundhu-oru-real-difference-async-function-a-call-pannradhu]

JS-la, async function-a call pannina, nee result-a `await` pannalum pannalanalum, adhu
udane run aaga start aagidum. Python-la, `async def` function-a call pannina adhu **run
aagave aagadhu** — inert-a irukura oru "coroutine" object matum create pannum, edhavadhu
actual-a adha await pannradhu allathu schedule pannradhu varaikkum:

```python
get_user()   # ippodikku edhuvum pannadhu! oru coroutine object matum create pannum
```

Oru plain script-oda top level-la actual-a idha run pannanum-na, Python-ku oru event loop
venum:

```python
import asyncio

result = asyncio.run(get_user())
```

Oru framework-kulla poitta apparam, nee usually `asyncio.run()` eluthave maatta — FastAPI-la,
nee route handlers-a `async def`-a matum eluthuva, FastAPI-oda sonthamana event loop adha
run pannikkum. "Await pannama edhuvum nadakkadhu" nu indha behavior than, JS-la irundhu
Python-ku varra bothu ippove internalize pannikanum, idhu than most common confusion.


# Phase 8 — async / await (/tanglish/docs/phase-8)



Estimated time: **\~45 minutes**. ⭐⭐⭐ — inniku ku last thing.

Indha concept unakku already JS-la irundhu theriyum — Python oda version almost same
keywords than use pannum.

## Goals [#goals]

```python
async def get_user():
    data = await fetch_data()
    return data
```

Puriyanum:

* `def` — oru normal function
* `async def` — oru asynchronous function
* `await` — async operation mudiyum varaikkum wait pannradhu

Naalaikku idhu genuinely podhum — idhu pathi innoru page, apparam inniku ku over.

## Cheat sheet [#cheat-sheet]

```text
JavaScript / TypeScript                    Python
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
function getUser() { }                     def get_user():

async function getUser() {                 async def get_user():
  const data = await fetchData();              data = await fetch_data()
  return data;                                 return data
}

await getUser()                             await get_user()   (async def-kulla matum)
```


# Database Connection (/tanglish/docs/fastapi/getting-started/database-connection)



`.env`-la unakku oru `DATABASE_URL` irukku. Ippo idha read panni database-ku oru
connection prepare pannura actual code venum. Idhu adhoda own file-la irukkum,
`database.py` — indha project-la database venum na vera every file, thaniya connect
pannadhu, idhula irundhu than import pannum.

## SQLAlchemy ku venum moonu pieces [#sqlalchemy-ku-venum-moonu-pieces]

Code paakura munnadi, nee enna build panra-nu therinjuko:

* **Engine** — database ku actual connection. Nee endha database oda pesuraan-nu idhukku
  theriyum, and background-la connections oda oru pool manage pannum.
* **Session** — idha database oda one conversation-nu nenachiko, queries run panna and
  changes save panna use pannuva. Aprom, per request oru puthu session create pannuva.
* **Base** — nee future lesson-la define pannura every database model (table) idhu
  irundhu than inherit pannum, oru base class.

## database.py [#databasepy]

```python title="database.py"
from sqlalchemy import create_engine; # to connect python and database
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker, declarative_base; # each session lets you talk to the database, declarative_base is base class for your orm models
from dotenv import load_dotenv;
import os;

load_dotenv()
DATABASE_URL = os.getenv("DATABASE_URL")

engine = create_engine(DATABASE_URL)
SessionLocal = sessionmaker(bind=engine, autoflush=False)
Base = declarative_base()
```

## Idha step-by-step paakalam [#idha-step-by-step-paakalam]

**`load_dotenv()`** unnoda `.env` file read pannum, adhoda values `os.getenv()`-la
irundhu available ah pannum — adhula irundhu edhachum read panna munnadi idhu run
aaganum.

**`os.getenv("DATABASE_URL")`** last lesson-la nee set up pannina exact connection
string-a read pannum.

**`create_engine(DATABASE_URL)`** andha connection string-a SQLAlchemy-ku kudukkum. Idhu
`mysql://` part-a parse pannum, adha pesa MySQL driver (`mysqlclient`, Project Setup-la
install pannirukkom) use pannanum-nu therinjikkum. Idha therinjuko: indha line actual ah
oru connection open pannadhu — engine lazy-ah connect aagum, adha first time actually use
pannumbodhu than.

**`sessionmaker(bind=engine, autoflush=False)`** kooda oru session create pannadhu — idhu
oru *factory* create pannum, `SessionLocal`, oru function, appuram edhavadhu code-ku
queries run panna real session venum-na nee adha call pannuva (`SessionLocal()`).
`bind=engine`, idhu create pannura ovvoru session-ayum mela irukkura engine oda tie
pannum; `autoflush=False` meaning, ovvoru query munnadi-yum SQLAlchemy pending changes-a
automatic ah database-ku send pannadhu — adhu eppo nadakkum-nu nee decide pannuva.

**`declarative_base()`** `Base` class create pannum. Future lesson-la nee Python class ah
define pannura every table, indha `Base`-la irundhu than inherit pannum, adhu than andha
classes database tables-nu SQLAlchemy-kku theriyum.

## Ippo enna nadakkala [#ippo-enna-nadakkala]

Indha file just connection-a *prepare* pannudhu — unnoda app-la ippo edhuvum idha use
pannadhu. Future lesson-la, nee oru chinna function ezhudhuva, adhu session venum na
ovvoru request-ku `SessionLocal()` session kudukkum, and request mudinjadhum automatic ah
close pannum. Ippozhukku, database-ku actual ah reach aaga unnoda project-kku venum ella
irukku.

<Callout title="For you, coming from Express/Nest">
  Idhu TypeORM `DataSource` illa Prisma `PrismaClient` set up pannura same role than — oru
  shared connection object, once create pannirukkum, adha app-oda rest-um import pannitu
  reuse pannum, per request oru puthu database connection open pannradhukku pathila.
  `engine` connection than, `SessionLocal` nee call panni oru usable client/query-runner
  vaanga use pannuva, and `Base`, future table classes ku TypeORM oda `@Entity()` base illa
  Prisma oda generated model types pannura role-a than play pannum.
</Callout>

## `database.py` ippo varaikkum [#databasepy-ippo-varaikkum]

```python title="database.py"
from sqlalchemy import create_engine; # to connect python and database
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker, declarative_base; # each session lets you talk to the database, declarative_base is base class for your orm models
from dotenv import load_dotenv;
import os;

load_dotenv()
DATABASE_URL = os.getenv("DATABASE_URL")

engine = create_engine(DATABASE_URL)
SessionLocal = sessionmaker(bind=engine, autoflush=False)
Base = declarative_base()
```


# Environment Configuration (/tanglish/docs/fastapi/getting-started/environment-configuration)



Web Fundamentals-la, database credentials maadhiri secrets oru user ku epozhume visible ah
irukka koodadhu-nu nee kathukiten. Adhula irundhu varura innoru rule irukku: avanga
unnoda source code-la kooda **hardcode** pannakoodadhu — code git-ku commit aagum,
teammates-oda share aagum, hosting providers-ku push aagum, and unnoda code paakura
everyone unnoda production database password paakanum-nu illa.

## Environment variables [#environment-variables]

Idhukku fix enna na, configuration-a unnoda code-ku **veliya** vekradhu, **environment
variables** ah — oru file-la ezhudradhu ku pathila, adha run pannura edhavadhu program
runtime-la unnoda program ku kudukkura values.

Local development-la, idha manage panna standard way oru `.env` file — `KEY=VALUE` pairs
irukkura oru plain text file, unnoda project root-la irukkum, unnoda program startup-la
idha read pannum. Idhu than last lesson-la nee install pannina `python-dotenv` package
ku exact ah purpose.

## Unnoda .env file create panradhu [#unnoda-env-file-create-panradhu]

Unnoda project root-la `.env`-nu peru vecha oru file create pannu, unnoda database
connection string add pannu:

```text title=".env"
DATABASE_URL=mysql://app_user:test@localhost:3306/todo
```

## Connection string read panradhu [#connection-string-read-panradhu]

Andha `DATABASE_URL` value-a **connection string**-nu solluvom — oru specific database ku
reach aaga venum na venum ella details-um oru single line-la pack panniruppanga. Idha
break pannunga:

```text
mysql://app_user:test@localhost:3306/todo
 │        │        │     │        │      │
 │        │        │     │        │      └─ database name
 │        │        │     │        └──────── port (3306 is MySQL's default)
 │        │        │     └───────────────── host (where the database server runs)
 │        │        └─────────────────────── password
 │        └──────────────────────────────── username
 └───────────────────────────────────────── which database engine to use
```

So indha line solradhu enna na: &#x2A;"indha machine-la run aagura oru MySQL server ku connect
pannu, port 3306-la, `app_user`-nu login pannu password `test` vechu, and `todo`-nu peru
vecha database use pannu."*

## `.env`-a epozhume git-ku commit pannadhu [#env-a-epozhume-git-ku-commit-pannadhu]

Unnoda `.env` file-la real credentials irukku — idha version control-ku **epozhume**
commit pannakoodadhu. Idha uடane `.gitignore`-la add pannu:

```text title=".gitignore"
.env
```

Project-a fresh ah set up pannura yaar-yaaravadhu, avanga own local `.env`-a avanga own
database details vechu create pannuvanga — idhu ovvoru developer oda local setup-la
part than, shared codebase oda part illa.

<Callout title="For you, coming from Express/Nest">
  Node-la irundha same pattern than: oru `.env` file, adhukku oru `.gitignore` entry, and
  startup-la `dotenv` idha load pannudhu. Ippa-idhirundhu change aagura ondru enna na, code-la
  oru value-a *epadi* read pannuraradhu than — Node oda `process.env.DATABASE_URL`, Python
  oda `os.getenv("DATABASE_URL")`-a maarum, adha next lesson-la than nee paapa.
</Callout>

## `.env` ippa varaikkum [#env-ippa-varaikkum]

```text title=".env"
DATABASE_URL=mysql://app_user:test@localhost:3306/todo
```

```text title=".gitignore"
.env
```


# Project Setup (/tanglish/docs/fastapi/getting-started/project-setup)



Edhavadhu FastAPI code ezhudura munnadi, unakku properly isolated aana oru project venum.
Idha set up panradhu than indha lesson.

## Virtual environment ஏன் venum? [#virtual-environment-ஏன்-venum]

Nee oru Python package install pannumbodhu, adhu normally unnoda machine-la **globally**
install aagum — just one project ku mattum illa. Project A ku package oda version 1 venum,
Project B ku version 2 venum-na, globally install panradhu ellam rendu project-um oru
odana conflict aagum.

Oru **virtual environment** idha fix pannum: idhu oru self-contained folder, adhula thani
Python copy and thani packages irukkum, unnoda system-wide Python-la irundhum, vera every
project-la irundhum completely separate ah.

<Callout title="For you, coming from Express/Nest">
  Node-la, idhu free-ah kidaikkum — every project ku automatic ah adhoda own `node_modules`
  folder irukkum. Python-la default ah idhu maadhiri edhuvum kidayathu, adhukkaga than indha
  extra step irukku: oru virtual environment than Python project-a, Node project oda
  `node_modules` maadhiri, per project isolated ah behave panna vekkum.
</Callout>

## Virtual environment create panradhu [#virtual-environment-create-panradhu]

Unnoda project folder kulla, idha run pannu:

```bash
python -m venv venv
```

Idhu `venv`-nu peru vecha oru new folder create pannum, adhula oru isolated Python
environment irukkum. (`venv` peru just oru convention — command peru `venv`, adhu create
pannura folder-ku technically edhavadhu peru vechikalam, aana almost everywhere `venv`-nu
than nee paapa.)

## Idha activate panradhu [#idha-activate-panradhu]

Virtual environment create panradhu podhathu illa — unnoda terminal-la idha **activate**
pannanum, so that `pip` (Python oda package installer) mattrum `python` rendume unnoda
system-wide environment ku pathila indha isolated environment-a than point pannum.

Windows-la:

```bash
.\venv\Scripts\activate
```

macOS/Linux-la:

```bash
source venv/bin/activate
```

Once activate pannina apparam, unnoda terminal prompt line start-la `(venv)`-nu kaatum —
adhu than confirmation, next-la nee install pannura edhuvum indha project oda isolated
environment-ku than pogudhu-nu, unnoda entire system-ku illa.

Indha project mela work panna, oru fresh terminal open pannum bodhu ella time-um virtual
environment-a again activate pannanum.

## Core dependencies install panradhu [#core-dependencies-install-panradhu]

Virtual environment active ah irukkumbodhu, FastAPI oda core toolkit install pannu:

```bash
pip install fastapi uvicorn sqlalchemy psycopg2-binary python-dotenv mysqlclient pydantic
```

Ovvondrum enna pannum-nu paakalam:

| Package           | Purpose                                                                          |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `fastapi`         | Web framework than — routing, request handling, validation                       |
| `uvicorn`         | Unnoda FastAPI app-a actual ah run pannura server                                |
| `sqlalchemy`      | Database vechu velai panna nee use pannura ORM                                   |
| `psycopg2-binary` | Oru PostgreSQL driver — SQLAlchemy Postgres oda pesa help pannum                 |
| `python-dotenv`   | `.env` file-la irundhu configuration load pannum                                 |
| `mysqlclient`     | Oru MySQL driver — SQLAlchemy MySQL oda pesa help pannum                         |
| `pydantic`        | Data validate pannum, unnoda API accept and return pannura schemas define pannum |

`pydantic` actually ah `fastapi`-oda part ah automatic ah install aagidum — nee strictly
adha separately list panna venam. Idha inga explicit ah include panradhu, en na nee adhula
irundhu directly and often import pannuva (idhu ஏன்-nu "What is FastAPI?"-la already
paatha), so idha FastAPI oda hidden detail-a vida adhoda own dependency-a nenaikardhu
better.

List-la PostgreSQL driver **and** MySQL driver rendume irukardha nee notice pannirupa.
SQLAlchemy-kku thaniya edhavadhu specific database oda pesa theriyathu — nee actual ah
connect pannura database matching oru driver adhukku venum. Indha course oda project
**MySQL** use pannudhu, so `mysqlclient` than ippo mukkiyam; `psycopg2-binary`, epavadhu
nee same project-a Postgres ku point pannina use aagum-nu apdiye vechirukkom.

Pause pannanum-nu irukkura one dhan &#x2A;*`uvicorn`**. FastAPI code thaniya server ah run
aagadhu — adhu just routes and logic describe pannura Python code than. `uvicorn` than
actual ah server process start pannum, requests-ku listen pannum, avatha unnoda FastAPI
app-ku feed pannum program.

<Callout title="For you, coming from Express/Nest">
  `uvicorn`, Node.js itself Express app ku pannura role-a, illa `nest start` unakku hood-ku
  kelaya pannura velaya than pannudhu — actual ah oru port open panni requests serve panna
  start pannura thing. `sqlalchemy`, TypeORM/Prisma/Sequelize (oru ORM) oda maps aagum,
  database drivers andha tools ku hood-la venum `pg` illa `mysql2` packages oda same idea
  than, and `python-dotenv`, Node oda `dotenv` package pannura exact same velai than pannum —
  peru kooda match aagudhu.
</Callout>


# What is FastAPI? (/tanglish/docs/fastapi/getting-started/what-is-fastapi)



Backend enna-nu ippo unakku *why* level-la puriyum. Ippo idhirundhu, nee ondha build panna
kathukapora — **FastAPI** vechu, APIs ezhuda specific ah build pannina oru Python framework.

## Oru micro framework [#oru-micro-framework]

FastAPI oru **micro framework** — idhu unakku oru small, focused core (routing, request
handling) kudukkum, rigid structure vecha oru huge all-in-one system illa. Nee unnoda own
project layout choose pannikalam, unakku actual ah venum na piece mattum add pannikalam.
Idhu vechu FastAPI **flexible** aagidhu: FastAPI unnoda code-a force panni "idhu than correct
way"-nu oru single method-la push pannadhu.

## Validation and docs, built-in ah irukku [#validation-and-docs-built-in-ah-irukku]

FastAPI innoru two libraries mela build aagirukku, avanga peru theriyardhu useful, epavum
avaanga kanpippanga:

* **Starlette** — FastAPI kula irukkura actual web layer-a handle pannudhu: requests
  receive pannradhu, correct function ku route pannradhu, response send pannradhu
* **Pydantic** — data validation handle pannudhu, Python Notes-la Phase 7-la nee
  kathukitta type hints vechu

Andha second point than periya deal. Unnoda endpoint data mela oru type hint ezhudhu, like
`age: int`, appuram FastAPI automatic ah:

1. Incoming data-a andha type mela **validate** pannum — `age: "abc"`-nu ஒரு request
   varradhuna, unnoda code run aaguradhukku munnadiye automatic ah reject pannidum
2. Adhukku **interactive documentation** **generate** pannum — every endpoint, adhukku
   expect aagura data, live-a try pannradhu ellathayum kaatura oru page, unakku extra
   code edhuvum ezhudama.

Andha second point genuinely FastAPI oda best features-la ondru: nee type hints vechu oru
endpoint define pannina second-la, free-ah oru working documentation page kidaikkum.

## Fast — genuinely fast [#fast--genuinely-fast]

"FastAPI" just oru peru illa. Idhu **Starlette** mela build aagirukkardhala, adhu Python
oda `async`/`await` (Python Notes Phase 8) support pannudhu, FastAPI oru very high volume
requests-a efficient ah handle pannum. Real benchmarks-la, idhu Node.js and Go-oda
competitive ah — sometimes andha rendaiyum vida fast ah — perform pannudhu, idhu oru Python
framework ku unusual than.

## Less code, more power [#less-code-more-power]

Type hints validation and documentation rendaiyum automatic ah drive pannradhala, separate,
hand-written validation schemas venum vera frameworks vida nee romba kammi repetitive code
than ezhudanum. Nee edholadhu unnoda data describe panna ezhuda pora type hints than, adhuve
*than* validation rules.

## ML and data apps ku perfect [#ml-and-data-apps-ku-perfect]

Machine learning and data science ku (NumPy, Pandas, PyTorch, etc.) Python than dominant
language. FastAPI Python nala irukkardhala, oru trained ML model illa oru data pipeline-a
edhuthu, adha API ah expose panna idhu oru natural way — cross-language bridge edhuvum
venaam.

## OpenAPI standard mela build aagirukku [#openapi-standard-mela-build-aagirukku]

FastAPI unnoda entire API ku automatic ah oru **OpenAPI** specification generate pannum —
every endpoint-a describe pannura oru industry-standard, machine-readable description. Idhu
than mேlе mention pannina interactive **Swagger UI** docs-a power pannudhu, nee build panna
edhavadhu FastAPI app-la `/docs`-la out of the box available irukkum, setup edhuvum venaam.

<Callout title="For you, coming from Express/Nest">
  Starlette-a, Express thane kudukkura HTTP layer oda FastAPI equivalent-a nenachikko, and
  Pydantic manual validation-a (`express-validator`, Zod) illa Nest oda DTOs +
  `class-validator`-a replace pannudhu-nu nenachikko — except idhu unnoda type hints-la
  irundhu automatic ah aagum, extra decorators illa nee hand-la ezhudura schemas illa. And
  auto-generated Swagger docs, Express-la `swagger-jsdoc`/`swagger-ui-express` illa Nest-la
  `@nestjs/swagger` vechu nee usually setup pannuradha replace pannudhu — FastAPI-la, nee
  ezhudura first endpoint-la irundhe idhu automatic ah irukkum.
</Callout>


# Create Todo — Your First Endpoint (/tanglish/docs/fastapi/todo-api/create-todo-endpoint)



Unakku oru model and oru schema irukku. Ippo actual ah requests serve panna time — `main.py`
than unnoda FastAPI app onna varradhu, and ippo than nee unnoda first real endpoint
ezhuduva.

## App [#app]

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI, Depends
from schemas import Todo as TodoSchema, TodoCreate
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
from database import SessionLocal, Base, engine
from models import Todo

Base.metadata.create_all(bind = engine)
app = FastAPI()
```

`app = FastAPI()` actual application object create pannudhu. Nee ezhudhura every route
indha `app`-la attach aagum, and `uvicorn` (Project Setup-la install pannirukkom) idha
than actual ah server ah run pannum.

## Table-a actual ah create panradhu [#table-a-actual-ah-create-panradhu]

`models.py` `todo` table-a describe pannina mattum than — idhu varaikkum database ku adha
actual ah create pannu-nu evanume sollala:

```python
Base.metadata.create_all(bind = engine)
```

`Base.metadata`-ku `Base`-la irundhu inherit pannura every model-um theriyum — indha case-la
`Todo`, `main.py` mேlе adha import pannurathala just register aaguchu. `create_all(bind =engine)` andha `engine`-oda database-a check pannum, and innum exist pannama irukkura
edhavadhu tables-a create pannum. App start aagum every time idha run pannalam safe ah
irukku: already irukkura tables-a touch pannadhu, missing-a mattum create pannum.

<Callout title="MySQL and column lengths">
  Oru model oda `String` columns length specify pannalanadha, indha exact line-la than nee
  idha find aaguva — MySQL every `VARCHAR` column ku explicit length require pannum, so
  `models.py`-la every `String` ku oru length (`String(200)`, example ku) kudukkura
  varaikkum `create_all`, `VARCHAR requires a length on dialect mysql`-nu fail aagum.
</Callout>

## Database session dependency [#database-session-dependency]

```python
# Dependency for DB session
def get_db():
    db = SessionLocal()
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.close()
```

Idhu than Database Connection lesson promise pannina function. Idhu oru **FastAPI
dependency** — oru function, oru route adhula irundhu edhavadhu vaanga kekkalam, adhu
epadi create aagum, epadi clean up aagum-nu worry pannama.

`return`-ku pathila `yield` use pannirukku-nu notice pannu (Python Notes-la Phase 5 and
8 generators and `async`/`await` cover pannirukku — idhu oru related idea than): `SessionLocal()`
call panradhu oru new session create pannum, `yield db` andha session-a kekkura route
ku hand pannum, and andha route mudinja apparam — successfully *illa* oru error-oda —
execution `yield`-ku apparam than resume aagum, and `finally: db.close()` rendu
ways-layum session close aagum-nu guarantee pannum.

## Depends — dependency-a route-la wire panradhu [#depends--dependency-a-route-la-wire-panradhu]

```python
def create(todo: TodoCreate, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
```

`db: Session = Depends(get_db)` FastAPI ku sollum: &#x2A;indha route run panna munnadi,
`get_db()`-a call pannu, adhoda `yield`-ku wait pannu, and adhu yield pannuradha `db`-nu
kudu.* Nee epozhume `get_db()`-a thaniya call panna maatta — FastAPI than adha unnoda
place-la call pannum, database session venum na every request ku.

## Route [#route]

```python
# POST - Create TODO
@app.post("/todos", response_model=TodoSchema)
def create(todo: TodoCreate, db:Session = Depends(get_db)):
    db_todo = Todo(**todo.dict())
    db.add(db_todo)
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(db_todo)
    return db_todo
```

**`@app.post("/todos", response_model=TodoSchema)`** — oru decorator, idhu indha
function-a `POST` requests-a `/todos`-ku handle panna register pannum. `response_model=
TodoSchema` FastAPI ku sollum, return aagura data enna shape-la validate and serialize
aaganum-nu — and idhu than indha endpoint ku unnoda auto-generated docs-la kooda kaanum.

**`todo: TodoCreate`** — request body. FastAPI incoming JSON-a read panni, `TodoCreate`
oda automatic ah validate pannum — first FastAPI lesson-la irundha same automatic
validation, ippo oru real request-ku apply pannirukku. Idhu than Creating the Todo Schema
lesson-oda payoff: **input** type (`TodoCreate`) ku `id` illa, so oru client adha send
panna mudiyadhu — aana **output** type (`response_model=TodoSchema`) ku irukku, en na
database mattum than adha assign panna mudiyum. Input and output, finally, rendu different
shapes use pannudhu, exactly plan pannina maadhiri.

**`db_todo = Todo(**todo.dict())`** — `todo` oru Pydantic schema instance; `.dict()` adha
plain dict ah maatrum, and `**` andha dict-a keyword arguments ah `Todo(...)`-la unpack
pannum — validated request data-a oru actual SQLAlchemy model instance ah maatrum, save
panna ready ah.

**`db.add(db_todo)`*&#x2A; new row-a stage pannum. &#x2A;*`db.commit()`*&#x2A; actual ah adha database-la
write pannum. &#x2A;*`db.refresh(db_todo)`** commit time-la database assign pannina values
vechu `db_todo`-a reload pannum — mukkiyamana, auto-generated `id`, idhu line run
aagardhukku munnadi `db_todo`-kku irukkadhu.

**`return db_todo`** — SQLAlchemy object-a directly return pannudhu, adha FastAPI back
JSON ah send panna munnadi `response_model` shape ah convert pannum.

<Callout title="For you, coming from Express/Nest">
  `Depends(get_db)` FastAPI oda dependency injection version than — oru Nest controller oda
  constructor-la inject pannirukkura oru Nest provider, illa unnoda handler run aaga munnadi
  `req.db` attach pannura oru Express middleware pannura same idea than. `@app.post("/todos")`
  Nest oda `@Post()` decorator illa Express oda `router.post()` pannura same job than. And
  `response_model`, oru Nest response DTO (illa manual `class-transformer` serialization)
  pannuradha pannum — unnoda internal database object-la irundhu separate ah, unnoda API-la
  irundhu exact ah enna leave aagum-nu control panradhu.
</Callout>

## `main.py` ippo varaikkum [#mainpy-ippo-varaikkum]

```python title="main.py"
from fastapi import FastAPI, Depends
from schemas import Todo as TodoSchema, TodoCreate
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
from database import SessionLocal, Base, engine
from models import Todo

Base.metadata.create_all(bind = engine)
app = FastAPI()

# Dependency for DB session
def get_db():
    db = SessionLocal()
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.close()


# POST - Create TODO
@app.post("/todos", response_model=TodoSchema)
def create(todo: TodoCreate, db:Session = Depends(get_db)):
    db_todo = Todo(**todo.dict())
    db.add(db_todo)
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(db_todo)
    return db_todo
```


# Creating the Todo Model (/tanglish/docs/fastapi/todo-api/creating-the-todo-model)



`database.py` unakku oru `Base` class kudutha, aana ippo varaikkum edhuvum adhula irundhu
inherit pannala — enga oru table describe pannala. Indha lesson mudhal ondra create
pannum: oru `Todo` model, indha course build panra app ku.

## Model-nu actual ah enna [#model-nu-actual-ah-enna]

Oru ORM-la, oru **model** solradhu oru Python class, adhu database table-la one table-a
represent pannum. Ovvoru class **attribute**-um andha table-la one **column**-a
represent pannum. Aprom nee indha class oda instances create panni actual rows create
pannuva — aana class itself just table oda *shape*-a describe pannum.

## models.py [#modelspy]

```python title="models.py"
from sqlalchemy import Column, Integer, String, Boolean;
from database import Base;

class Todo(Base):
    __tablename__ = "todo"
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True, index=True)
    title = Column(String(200), nullable=False)
    description = Column(String(500))
    completed = Column(Boolean, default=False)
```

## Idha step-by-step paakalam [#idha-step-by-step-paakalam]

**`class Todo(Base):`** — (`database.py`-la irundhu) `Base`-la irundhu inherit
panradhu than SQLAlchemy ku sollum "indha class oru database table-a describe
pannudhu"-nu, normal Python class illa-nu.

**`__tablename__ = "todo"`** — database-la SQLAlchemy use pannura actual table name.

**Ovvoru `Column(...)`**-um one field describe pannum:

* `id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True, index=True)` — ovvoru row-a uniquely identify
  pannura oru whole number. `primary_key=True` meaning, database adha unique-nu
  guarantee pannum, and adha automatic ah fill pannum (1, 2, 3, ...) — nee epozhume
  thaniya set pannama.
* `title = Column(String(200), nullable=False)` — text, 200 characters ku cap
  pannirukku, and `nullable=False` meaning every todo ku title **mandatory ah** irukanum —
  title illama oru row-a database reject pannidum.
* `description = Column(String(500))` — idhu kooda text than, 500 characters ku cap
  pannirukku, aana optional: `nullable` set pannalanadha, default ah `True`-nu irukkum,
  so oru todo description illama exist pannalam.
* `completed = Column(Boolean, default=False)` — true/false, and every new todo, nee
  vera edhavadhu sollala na `False`-nu start aagum.

<Callout title="Why String needs a length here">
  MySQL oda `VARCHAR` type ku **explicit maximum length** vendiyadhu than — chila vera
  databases pola illa, adhu length illama oru text column create panna simply let pannadhu.
  Length-a vittuduna, SQLAlchemy actual ah indha table create panna try pannumbodhu than nee
  enna wrong-nu notice pannuva, `VARCHAR requires a length on dialect mysql`-nu adhu fail
  aagum. Field ku edhu makes sense-nu andha limit-a pick pannu — 200 illa 500 idhula special
  edhuvum illa, title and description ku reasonable caps than.
</Callout>

## Idhu ippo varaikkum panradhu illa [#idhu-ippo-varaikkum-panradhu-illa]

Indha class ezhudradhu, unnoda actual MySQL database-la `todo` table create pannadhu —
adha just *describe* pannudhu than. SQLAlchemy ku table-a actual ah create pannu-nu
sollradhu, oru separate step, adhu next varum.

<Callout title="For you, coming from Express/Nest">
  Idhu than TypeORM `@Entity()` class oda `@Column()` decorators, illa oru Mongoose
  schema pannura same job — table oda shape-a describe pannura oru class, adha ORM aprom
  SQL generate panna use pannum. `primary_key=True`, TypeORM oda
  `@PrimaryGeneratedColumn()` same idea than, and `nullable=False`, oru column `NOT NULL`
  mark panradhu (illa Mongoose schema-la oru required field) match pannum.
</Callout>

## `models.py` ippo varaikkum [#modelspy-ippo-varaikkum]

```python title="models.py"
from sqlalchemy import Column, Integer, String, Boolean;
from database import Base;

class Todo(Base):
    __tablename__ = "todo"
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True, index=True)
    title = Column(String(200), nullable=False)
    description = Column(String(500))
    completed = Column(Boolean, default=False)
```


# Creating the Todo Schema (/tanglish/docs/fastapi/todo-api/creating-the-todo-schema)



`models.py`, unnoda database-la `todo` table describe pannudhu. Ippo unakku vera edhavadhu
venum: data **unnoda API-la in and out** HTTP mela travel pannumbodhu adhu epadi kaanum-nu
describe panna oru vazhi. Adhu than oru **schema** — and purpose-a vechu, idhu model-la
irundhu oru separate concept than.

## Model-a enne reuse pannakoodadha? [#model-a-enne-reuse-pannakoodadha]

"Naan already oru `Todo`-a describe pannirukken, enna adha again describe pannanum" nu
nenaikardhu tempting than. Idhu ஏன் work aagadhu-nu chila real reasons:

* **Different situations ku different fields.** Oru client oru todo *create* pannumbodhu,
  avanga `id` send panna venaam — database than adha assign pannum, and adhu innum exist
  pannala. Aana API oru todo *return* pannumbodhu, `id` include aaganum-nu venum. Oru
  shape rendaiyum represent panna mudiyadhu.
* **Unnoda API-la irundhu enna leave aagum-nu control.** Oru database model-la, client
  epozhume paakka koodadha fields kooda irukkalam. Actual ah enna back send aagum-nu
  explicit ah decide pannura place than schema.
* **Different jobs ku different tools.** `models.py`, SQLAlchemy oda `Base` use pannudhu
  — idhu database oda pesa build pannirukku. Schemas **Pydantic**-oda `BaseModel` use
  pannum — first FastAPI lesson-la irundha same validation library — and FastAPI actual
  ah idha than requests validate panna and unnoda API docs generate panna use pannum.

## schemas.py [#schemaspy]

```python title="schemas.py"
from pydantic import BaseModel

class TodoBase(BaseModel):
    title: str
    description: str | None = None
    completed: bool = False

# create
class TodoCreate(TodoBase):
    pass

# response
class Todo(TodoBase):
    id: int
    class Config:
        orm_mode = True # for automatic json parsing
```

## Idha step-by-step paakalam [#idha-step-by-step-paakalam]

**`TodoBase`** oru todo take pannalam-nu irukkura every shape-um share pannura
fields-a vechirukku — `title`, `description`, and `completed`, ovvondrum once mattum
ezhudhi. Kelu irukkura rendu schemas-um idha mela build aagum. `completed`-ku oru
default (`False`) irukkardhala, adhu inherit aagura endha place-layum optional than — oru
client adha entirely leave out pannalam, still oru valid todo kidaikkum.

**`TodoCreate(TodoBase)`** oru client puthu todo create panna send pannuradhu. `TodoBase`
vida idhu edhuvum extra add pannala — client provide panna allowed aana ella something-um
(`title`, `description`, optionally `completed`) already adhula irukku. Idha adhoda own
class ah vekkardhu, meaning aprom creation-only fields add pannalam, todo back read
panna use pannura shape-a touch pannama.

**`Todo(TodoBase)`** API **back** send pannuradhu. Idhu `id` add pannum — oru todo
actual ah database-la save aana apparam than exist pannura field, adhukku than idhu
`TodoCreate`-la illa.

**`class Config: orm_mode = True`** idha unnoda SQLAlchemy model-oda back connect
pannura detail. Default ah, oru Pydantic schema oru plain dict-la irundhu build aagum-nu
expect pannum. `orm_mode = True` adhukku sollum "matching attributes vecha oru object-la
irundhum idha build pannalam" — adhu than exactly oru `models.Todo` instance. Idhu than
oru SQLAlchemy object-a route-la irundhu straight ah return panna, and FastAPI adha
automatic ah, field by field, indha schema ah convert panna vidum — comment-la irukkura
"automatic json parsing".

<Callout title="Pydantic version note">
  `orm_mode` idha setting ku Pydantic v1 name than. Newer Pydantic versions idha
  `from_attributes`-nu rename pannirukku (`model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)`
  vazhi set pannuvanga), aana rendume exact same job than pannum — oru project use pannura
  Pydantic version-a vechu, nee edhavadhu spelling paakkalam.
</Callout>

## Rendu `Todo`s, purpose vechu [#rendu-todos-purpose-vechu]

`models.py`-la oru `Todo` class irukku, ippo `schemas.py`-lam kooda ondru irukku-nu
notice pannu. Idhu intentional than and completely safe than — avanga separate files-la
irukkuranga, so nee avatha `models.Todo` and `schemas.Todo`-nu refer pannuva. Idhu oru
common pattern than, nee once paatha udane recognize pannuva:

|                     | `models.py` (SQLAlchemy) | `schemas.py` (Pydantic)               |
| ------------------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------- |
| Describe pannuradhu | Oru database table       | Oru API request/response shape        |
| Yaar use pannuranga | ORM, MySQL oda pesa      | FastAPI, validate and serialize panna |
| Base class          | `Base`                   | `BaseModel`                           |

<Callout title="For you, coming from Express/Nest">
  Idhu than exactly Nest already unnaya push pannura separation: oru `CreateTodoDto`
  (`class-validator` vechu validate pannirukku) vs oru TypeORM `@Entity()` — "API accept /
  return pannuradhu" "table epadi irukku"-la irundhu separate ah vekkardhu. Plain
  Express-la, oru Zod illa Joi validation schema vs oru Sequelize/TypeORM model-oda
  difference than idhu. Oru Pydantic schema, FastAPI oda DTO version than — same idea,
  same exist pannura reason.
</Callout>

## `schemas.py` ippo varaikkum [#schemaspy-ippo-varaikkum]

```python title="schemas.py"
from pydantic import BaseModel

class TodoBase(BaseModel):
    title: str
    description: str | None = None
    completed: bool = False

# create
class TodoCreate(TodoBase):
    pass

# response
class Todo(TodoBase):
    id: int
    class Config:
        orm_mode = True # for automatic json parsing
```


# Delete Todo (/tanglish/docs/fastapi/todo-api/delete-todo)



Last CRUD operation: oru todo-a entirely remove panradhu.

## Route [#route]

```python
#DELETE - Delete Todo
@app.delete("/todos/{todo_id}")
def delete_todo(todo_id:int,  db:Session = Depends(get_db)):
    todo = db.query(Todo).filter(Todo.id == todo_id).first()
    if not todo:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Todo not found")
    db.delete(todo)
    db.commit()
    return {"message":"Todo deleted successfully"}
```

## Idha step-by-step paakalam [#idha-step-by-step-paakalam]

**`@app.delete("/todos/{todo_id}")`** — `DELETE` method than, oru single todo fetch illa
update panradhu-la irundha same path parameter pattern. Indha time `response_model`
edhuvum illa-nu notice pannu — oru todo delete aana apparam, response-a shape panna
`Todo` edhuvum illa.

**Find pannu, illana 404** — Fetch a Single Todo and Update Todo-la irundha same
lookup-then-check pattern than: id vechu query pannu, and onnume match aagalana
`HTTPException(404, ...)` raise pannu. Ippozhukku idha exact ah pattern-a three
times ezhudhirukka — idha future-la, `Depends()` epadi work aagum-nu unakku comfortable
aana apparam, oru single shared dependency-la pull panna mudiyum-nu oru good sign than.

**`db.delete(todo)`** row-a removal ku stage pannum — `db.add()&#x60;-oda delete equivalent
than. &#x2A;*`db.commit()`** actual ah adha database-la irundhu remove pannum.

**`return {"message":"Todo deleted successfully"}`** — oru plain Python dict than, `Todo`
illa. Indha route-la `response_model` illama irukkardhala, FastAPI nee return pannura
edhuvum directly JSON ah serialize pannum. Idha maadhiri oru chinna confirmation message
return panradhu, oru delete endpoint ku normal choice than — back kudukka meaningful ah
onnume illa.

<Callout title="For you, coming from Express/Nest">
  `db.delete(todo)` + `db.commit()`, Sequelize-la `todo.destroy()`, TypeORM-la
  `repository.remove(todo)`, illa Prisma-la `prisma.todo.delete()` pannura same job than.
  And deleted resource-ku pathila plain `{"message": "..."}` return panradhu, Express-la
  `res.json({ message: 'Deleted' })` pannura exact ah same thing than — idhula FastAPI
  specific ah edhuvum illa.
</Callout>

## `main.py` ippo varaikkum [#mainpy-ippo-varaikkum]

Ippo every CRUD operation-um place-la irukku: create, read all, read one, update,
delete.

```python title="main.py"
from fastapi import FastAPI, Depends, HTTPException
from schemas import Todo as TodoSchema, TodoCreate
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
from database import SessionLocal, Base, engine
from models import Todo

Base.metadata.create_all(bind = engine)
app = FastAPI()

# Dependency for DB session
def get_db():
    db = SessionLocal()
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.close()


# POST - Create TODO
@app.post("/todos", response_model=TodoSchema)
def create(todo: TodoCreate, db:Session = Depends(get_db)):
    db_todo = Todo(**todo.dict())
    db.add(db_todo)
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(db_todo)
    return db_todo

# GET - All Todos
@app.get("/todos", response_model = list[TodoSchema])
def read_todos(db:Session = Depends(get_db)):
    return db.query(Todo).all()

@app.get("/todos/{todo_id}", response_model = TodoSchema)
def read_todo(todo_id: int,db:Session = Depends(get_db)):
    todo = db.query(Todo).filter(Todo.id == todo_id).first()
    if not todo:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Todo not found")
    return todo

# PUT - Update Todo
@app.put("/todos/{todo_id}", response_model=TodoSchema)
def update_todo(todo_id:int, updated: TodoCreate, db:Session = Depends(get_db)):
    todo = db.query(Todo).filter(Todo.id == todo_id).first()
    if not todo:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Todo not found")
    for key, value in updated.dict().items():
        setattr(todo, key, value)
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(todo)
    return todo

#DELETE - Delete Todo
@app.delete("/todos/{todo_id}")
def delete_todo(todo_id:int,  db:Session = Depends(get_db)):
    todo = db.query(Todo).filter(Todo.id == todo_id).first()
    if not todo:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Todo not found")
    db.delete(todo)
    db.commit()
    return {"message":"Todo deleted successfully"}
```


# Fetch All Todos (/tanglish/docs/fastapi/todo-api/fetch-all-todos)



Todo create panradhu work aaguthu, next endpoint avatha back read pannum — database-la
irukkura every todo-a.

## Route [#route]

```python
# GET - All Todos
@app.get("/todos", response_model = list[TodoSchema])
def read_todos(db:Session = Depends(get_db)):
    return db.query(Todo).all()
```

## Idha step-by-step paakalam [#idha-step-by-step-paakalam]

**`@app.get("/todos", ...)`** — `create`-la irundha same decorator pattern than, aana
`@app.post`-ku pathila `@app.get`. Oru `GET` request oru request body kondu varadhu, adhukku
than `create` maadhiri `read_todos`, `todo` parameter edukkadhu.

**`response_model = list[TodoSchema]`** — Python Notes Phase 7-la irundha container type
hints, ippo real velai pannudhu: `list[TodoSchema]` FastAPI ku sollum "response oru list,
adhula every item-um oru `TodoSchema`". Single `response_model=TodoSchema` oru item
handle pannura maadhiri than, return aagura list-la irukkura every item-um idhu validate
and serialize pannum.

**`db:Session = Depends(get_db)`** — `create` route-la irundha same database dependency
than. Data read panna kooda oru session venum, write pannina maadhiri exact ah.

**`db.query(Todo).all()`** — SQLAlchemy oda query syntax: `db.query(Todo)` `todo` table ku
oru query start pannum, and `.all()` adha run panni, match aana every row-a, `Todo`
(SQLAlchemy) instances oda oru list ah return pannum. Filtering edhuvum add pannalanadha,
meaning table-la irukkura every row-um.

**`return db.query(Todo).all()`** — `create` maadhiri than: SQLAlchemy objects-a directly
return pannudhu, and (schema lesson-la irundha) `orm_mode` than FastAPI ku ovvondrayum
automatic ah oru `TodoSchema` ah convert panna vidum.

<Callout title="For you, coming from Express/Nest">
  `db.query(Todo).all()`, Sequelize-la `Model.findAll()`, TypeORM-la `repository.find()`,
  illa Prisma-la `prisma.todo.findMany()` pannura same job than — "every row-a kudu",
  edhuvum filter apply pannama. Oru single todo id vechu fetch panna varumbodhu, idha nee
  actual filters vechu narrow down pannuva.
</Callout>

## `main.py` ippo varaikkum [#mainpy-ippo-varaikkum]

```python title="main.py"
from fastapi import FastAPI, Depends
from schemas import Todo as TodoSchema, TodoCreate
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
from database import SessionLocal, Base, engine
from models import Todo

Base.metadata.create_all(bind = engine)
app = FastAPI()

# Dependency for DB session
def get_db():
    db = SessionLocal()
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.close()


# POST - Create TODO
@app.post("/todos", response_model=TodoSchema)
def create(todo: TodoCreate, db:Session = Depends(get_db)):
    db_todo = Todo(**todo.dict())
    db.add(db_todo)
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(db_todo)
    return db_todo

# GET - All Todos
@app.get("/todos", response_model = list[TodoSchema])
def read_todos(db:Session = Depends(get_db)):
    return db.query(Todo).all()
```


# Fetch a Single Todo (/tanglish/docs/fastapi/todo-api/fetch-single-todo)



Every todo fetch panradhu useful, aana unakku **one specific** todo-a kooda fetch panna
venum — adhoda id vechu. Idhu rendu puthu ideas introduce pannum: URL-la irundhu directly
oru value read panradhu, and edhavadhu exist pannala-na client ku clear ah sollradhu.

## Route [#route]

```python
@app.get("/todos/{todo_id}", response_model = TodoSchema)
def read_todo(todo_id: int,db:Session = Depends(get_db)):
    todo = db.query(Todo).filter(Todo.id == todo_id).first()
    if not todo:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Todo not found")
    return todo
```

## Path parameters [#path-parameters]

**`@app.get("/todos/{todo_id}", ...)`** — path-la irukkura `{todo_id}` oru **path
parameter** — enga vandhalum andha value ku match aagura oru placeholder. `/todos/5`
visit pannu, `todo_id` `5`-nu aagum.

**`def read_todo(todo_id: int, ...)`** — parameter name path-la irukkura `{todo_id}`-oda
exact ah match aaganum. FastAPI URL-la irundhu directly value-a read pannum, and nee
annotate pannura endha type-um (inga `int`) adha convert pannum — adha vazhi validate
pannikittu. `/todos/abc` visit pannu, FastAPI automatic ah request-a reject pannidum,
unnoda function run aaga munnadi than, en na `"abc"` oru valid `int` illa.

## Query filter panradhu [#query-filter-panradhu]

Fetch All Todos-la `.all()` use pannirundhom — filtering edhuvum illama every row. Indha
route ku exactly one venum:

```python
todo = db.query(Todo).filter(Todo.id == todo_id).first()
```

**`.filter(Todo.id == todo_id)`** query-a `id&#x60; column match aagura rows-ku narrow down
pannum. &#x2A;*`.first()`** query-a run panni, match aana first row mattum return pannum — illa
onnume match aagalanadha, error raise pannuradhukku pathila `None` return pannum.

## "Not found" handle panradhu [#not-found-handle-panradhu]

```python
if not todo:
    raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Todo not found")
```

`.first()` no match ku `None` return pannurathala, and `None` falsy aanadhala, `if not
todo:` "onnume find aagala na"-nu read aagum. `HTTPException` solradhu FastAPI oru `raise`-a
(Python Notes Phase 6) oru real HTTP error response ah maatrura vazhi: idha raise
pannradhu function-a stop panni, client ku oru real `404` status code send pannum,
`{"detail": "Todo not found"}` body oda — unnoda API confusing edhavadhu return
pannuradhukku, illa crash aaguradhukku pathila.

<Callout title="For you, coming from Express/Nest">
  Oru FastAPI path parameter, Express oda `req.params.id` illa Nest oda `@Param('id') id:
  number` pannura same idea than — except FastAPI adha type-a kooda automatic ah convert
  and validate pannum, Nest oda pipes pannura maadhiri. `HTTPException(status_code=404,
  ...)` raise panradhu, Nest-la `throw new HttpException(...)` illa Express-la hand-la
  ezhudhura `res.status(404).json({...})` exact ah than — oru specific error response oda
  oru request-a early ah end panna oru clean way.
</Callout>

## `main.py` ippo varaikkum [#mainpy-ippo-varaikkum]

```python title="main.py"
from fastapi import FastAPI, Depends, HTTPException
from schemas import Todo as TodoSchema, TodoCreate
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from models import Todo

        yield db
    finally:
        db.close()


# POST - Create TODO
```
