```python title="main.py"
    db_todo = Todo(**todo.dict())
    db.add(db_todo)
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(db_todo)
    return db_todo

# GET - All Todos
@app.get("/todos", response_model = list[TodoSchema])
def read_todos(db:Session = Depends(get_db)):
    return db.query(Todo).all()

@app.get("/todos/{todo_id}", response_model = TodoSchema)
def read_todo(todo_id: int,db:Session = Depends(get_db)):
    todo = db.query(Todo).filter(Todo.id == todo_id).first()
    if not todo:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Todo not found")
    return todo
```


# Running & Testing Your API (/tanglish/docs/fastapi/todo-api/running-and-testing)



Unakku oru working endpoint irukku. Ippo actual ah server-a run panni try pannura time.

## Server start panradhu [#server-start-panradhu]

```bash
uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --reload
```

Idha break pannu paakalam:

* **`uvicorn`** — Project Setup-la nee install pannina server program. Ninaivula
  vechuko: unnoda FastAPI code thaniya run aagadhu; `uvicorn` than actual ah server
  process start pannum.
* **`main:app`** — `uvicorn`-ku unnoda application enga irukku-nu sollum: `main` module
  (unnoda `main.py`), and adhula irukkura `app` variable (`app = FastAPI()`).
* **`--host 0.0.0.0`** — unnoda own machine mattum illa, every network interface-um
  listen pannu. `127.0.0.1` (default) unnoda own computer-la irundhu vandha connections
  mattum accept pannum; `0.0.0.0` unnoda network-la irukkura vera devices-um idha reach
  panna vidum — unnoda phone-la irundhu test panna useful.
* **`--port 8000`** — endha port-la listen pannanum. Unnoda API ippo
  `http://localhost:8000`-la reachable ah irukku.
* **`--reload`** — nee oru code change save pannumbodhu ella time-um automatic ah server-a
  restart pannum. Development-la idha constantly use pannu — idhu illama rarely irukka
  venum-nu nee nenaipa. &#x2A;*Production-la idha epozhume use pannadhu.**

## Idha test panradhu — interactive docs [#idha-test-panradhu--interactive-docs]

"What is FastAPI?"-la irundhu recall pannu: every FastAPI app automatic ah interactive
API docs vaangum. Ippo nee avatha actual ah use panna mudiyum — unnoda browser-a idha
open pannu:

```text
http://localhost:8000/docs
```

Nee ezhudhina every endpoint-um inga list aagirukkum — ippozhukku, `POST /todos`. Idha
expand pannu, **Try it out** click pannu, oru sample `title` and `description` fill
pannu, and oru real request send pannu — straight ah browser-la irundhu, separate tool
edhuvum venaam. Unnoda API back send pannina actual response-a nee paapa, unnoda database
assign pannina `id`-um including.

<Callout title="For you, coming from Express/Nest">
  Express-la, oru endpoint test panna Postman illa `curl`-ku poga, en na built-in ah edhuvum
  illa. Nest `@nestjs/swagger` vechu close ah kudukkum, aana adhukku manual setup venum —
  every DTO and route mela decorators. FastAPI-la, nee unnoda first endpoint ezhudhina
  second-le indha page exist pannudhu, nee already ezhudhina same type hints and schemas-la
  irundhu generate aagirukku.
</Callout>


# Update Todo — PUT vs PATCH (/tanglish/docs/fastapi/todo-api/update-todo)



Oru resource update panradhu rendu different things solllalam: completely replace
panradhu, illa just one field change panradhu. HTTP-kku ovvondrukkum oru separate method
irukku — `PUT` and `PATCH` — indha lesson rendaiyum cover pannum.

## PUT — whole thing-a replace pannu [#put--whole-thing-a-replace-pannu]

```python
# PUT - Update Todo
@app.put("/todos/{todo_id}", response_model=TodoSchema)
def update_todo(todo_id:int, updated: TodoCreate, db:Session = Depends(get_db)):
    todo = db.query(Todo).filter(Todo.id == todo_id).first()
    if not todo:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Todo not found")
    for key, value in updated.dict().items():
        setattr(todo, key, value)
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(todo)
    return todo
```

Lookup and not-found handling Fetch a Single Todo-la nee already paatha exact ah than.
Puthusa irukkura ondru:

**`updated: TodoCreate`** — todo create pannina schema-a reuse pannirukkom. Idhu
intentional than: `TodoCreate`-ku `title` require aagum, so indha route call pannura oru
client oru full, complete todo **mandatory ah** send pannanum — adhu than `PUT` oda
definition.

**`for key, value in updated.dict().items(): setattr(todo, key, value)`** — incoming
data-la irukkura every field mela idhu loop pannum, and Python oda built-in `setattr
(object, name, value)` vechu `todo`-la adha one field at a time set pannum. `todo.title =
value`, `todo.description = value`, and `todo.completed = value` ah separately ezhudhura
maadhiri than — every field ku repeat pannama.

**`db.commit()` / `db.refresh(todo)` / `return todo`** — changes-a save pannum, instance-a
reload pannum, and adha return pannum, todo create pannura same pattern than.

## PATCH — send pannina mattum change pannu [#patch--send-pannina-mattum-change-pannu]

Mேlе irukkura `PUT` epozhume every field-a overwrite pannum, en na `TodoCreate`-ku
avanga ellam mandatory ah venum. `PATCH` opposite case ku than: oru client **just one
field** update pannanum — solllu, oru todo-a `completed`-nu mark panna — title and
description-a again resend pannama.

Idhukku every field optional ah irukkura oru schema venum:

```python title="schemas.py (new)"
class TodoUpdate(BaseModel):
    title: str | None = None
    description: str | None = None
    completed: bool | None = None
```

And actual ah provide pannina fields-a mattum touch pannura oru route:

```python title="main.py (new)"
# PATCH - Partially Update Todo
@app.patch("/todos/{todo_id}", response_model=TodoSchema)
def partial_update_todo(todo_id: int, updated: TodoUpdate, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    todo = db.query(Todo).filter(Todo.id == todo_id).first()
    if not todo:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Todo not found")
    for key, value in updated.dict(exclude_unset=True).items():
        setattr(todo, key, value)
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(todo)
    return todo
```

Idha actual ah oru *partial&#x2A; update ah work pannura detail than &#x2A;*`exclude_unset=True`**.
Idhu illama, `updated.dict()` `TodoUpdate`-la irukkura every field-um include pannirukkum
— and client send pannama vidra edhavadhu field database-la `None`-nu kaanum, adha wipe
pannidum. `exclude_unset=True` meaning "client actual ah request-la send pannina fields
mattum include pannu" — so `{"completed": true}` just `completed`-a update pannum, and
`title` and `description`-a untouched ah vidum.

<Callout title="This route isn't in your project yet">
  Earlier lessons vida different ah, indha `TodoUpdate` schema and `partial_update_todo`
  route indha topic ku oru worked example than, unnoda `fastapi-todo` project-la irundhu
  edutha code illa — `PATCH` support venum-na, idha nee thaniya add pannu, appuram enakku
  sollu, naan indha lesson-a unnoda actual code oda sync pannuren, vera every topic
  maadhiri than.
</Callout>

## PUT vs PATCH [#put-vs-patch]

|                         | `PUT`                                 | `PATCH`                             |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| Meaning                 | Entire resource-a replace pannu       | Adhula part-a update pannu          |
| Client enna send pannum | Every field                           | Change aagura fields mattum         |
| Schema ku venum         | Required fields (`TodoCreate`)        | Every field optional (`TodoUpdate`) |
| Omitted field           | Overwrite aagum (usually clear aagum) | Unchanged ah irukkum                |

Idha remember panna oru useful way: &#x2A;*PUT solradhu "idha the whole new version"; PATCH
solradhu "idha change aana thing."**

<Callout title="For you, coming from Express/Nest">
  Nest already `@Put()` vs `@Patch()` decorators vechu, illa Express oda `router.put()` vs
  `router.patch()` vechu pannura same distinction than — HTTP methods and avanga meaning
  change aagadhu. Different ah irukkuradhu enna na, FastAPI rendu separate Pydantic schemas
  (required vs every field `Optional`) mela lean pannudhu, distinction enforce panna — oru
  DTO oda completeness-a hand-la validate pannradhukku pathila.
</Callout>

## `main.py` ippo varaikkum [#mainpy-ippo-varaikkum]

Idhu unnoda actual project-a reflect pannudhu — `PUT` route mattum. Mேlе irukkura
`PATCH` example idhula include pannala, en na idhu innum `fastapi-todo`-la part illa.

```python title="main.py"
from fastapi import FastAPI, Depends, HTTPException
from schemas import Todo as TodoSchema, TodoCreate
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
from database import SessionLocal, Base, engine
from models import Todo

Base.metadata.create_all(bind = engine)
app = FastAPI()

# Dependency for DB session
def get_db():
    db = SessionLocal()
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.close()


# POST - Create TODO
@app.post("/todos", response_model=TodoSchema)
def create(todo: TodoCreate, db:Session = Depends(get_db)):
    db_todo = Todo(**todo.dict())
    db.add(db_todo)
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(db_todo)
    return db_todo

# GET - All Todos
@app.get("/todos", response_model = list[TodoSchema])
def read_todos(db:Session = Depends(get_db)):
    return db.query(Todo).all()

@app.get("/todos/{todo_id}", response_model = TodoSchema)
def read_todo(todo_id: int,db:Session = Depends(get_db)):
    todo = db.query(Todo).filter(Todo.id == todo_id).first()
    if not todo:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Todo not found")
    return todo

# PUT - Update Todo
@app.put("/todos/{todo_id}", response_model=TodoSchema)
def update_todo(todo_id:int, updated: TodoCreate, db:Session = Depends(get_db)):
    todo = db.query(Todo).filter(Todo.id == todo_id).first()
    if not todo:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Todo not found")
    for key, value in updated.dict().items():
        setattr(todo, key, value)
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(todo)
    return todo
```


# Putting It Together — How Does YouTube Work? (/tanglish/docs/fastapi/web-fundamentals/how-youtube-works)



Ippo pieces unakku theriyum: client, backend, database. Indha lesson avatha oru real
example vechu together vekkum, ellarukkum already puriyum — **YouTube** — and andha vazhi,
nee innum meet pannama irukkura innoru piece-a kandupidikkum.

## Rendu romba different kind of data [#rendu-romba-different-kind-of-data]

Oru single video ku YouTube track pannanum-na enna ellam venum-nu nenachiko:

* Adhoda **title**, **description**, **upload date**, **view count**, **like count**
* Adhoda **comments**, and yaar post pannaan-nu
* **Actual video file** itself — and adhoda thumbnail image

Mudhal rendu, nee ippo dhaan kathukitta thing than: database tables-la rows. Oru
`title` column and oru `view_count` column vecha `videos` table perfect ah fit aagum.

Aana andha video file? Oru single video hundreds of megabytes, gigabytes kooda irukalam.
Idhu oru real question raise pannum:

**Video file-a kooda database-la, edhavadhu column-la save panna mudiyadha?**

## Databases idhukku ஏன் build aagala [#databases-idhukku-ஏன்-build-aagala]

Technically, chila databases large binary blobs store panna mudiyum — aana idha YouTube
scale-la panradhu bad idea:

* Databases build aagirukku, *many small rows* mela fast ah search, filter, sort panna —
  yaarum *contents*-a "search" panna edhukkume vendaam, huge files-a hold panna illa
* Every raw video file-a kooda hold pannura oru database massive ah aagidum, backups,
  replication, and queries ellame dramatically slow aagidum
* Databases oru large file-a millions of viewers ku onnu-la **stream** panna design
  aagala — adhu completely different kind of workload than

So real applications rendaiyum split pannuvanga:

<Mermaid
  chart="
graph TD
A[Everything about a video] --> B[Structured data:<br/>title, description,<br/>views, comments]
A --> C[The actual files:<br/>video, thumbnail]
B --> D[(Database)]
C --> E[Storage Server]
"
/>

## Storage server-a meet pannu [#storage-server-a-meet-pannu]

Oru **storage server** (often *object storage*-nu solluvanga — AWS S3 illa Google Cloud
Storage nenachiko) oru service, adhoda mattum velai, large files-a efficient ah store
panradhum, serve panradhum than. Database epozhume video itself-a hold pannadhu — adhu
storage server-la andha file enge irukku-nu oru **reference** mattum than hold pannum
(oru URL illa file path).

Large platforms avanga storage-oda munnadi oru **CDN** (Content Delivery Network) kooda
vekkuvanga — popular videos oda copies, world ellam irukkura viewers ku physically close
aana servers-la cache aagum, so India-la irukkura oruthanukku, world oda vera side-la
irukkura server-la irundhu every byte fetch panna venaam. Idha nee thaniya build panna
venaam; idhu nee connect pannura oru service than, database ku nee epadi connect
pannuvayo, adha maadhiri than.

## Full picture [#full-picture]

<Mermaid
  chart="
graph LR
A[Client<br/>browser or app] -- requests --> B[Backend]
B -- structured data --> C[(Database)]
B -- file references --> D[Storage Server + CDN]
D -. video/image bytes .-> A
"
/>

## Step-by-step: video upload panradhu [#step-by-step-video-upload-panradhu]

1. Nee client-la oru video file select panni upload click pannu.
2. Client andha file-a **backend**-ku send pannum.
3. Backend actual video file-a **storage server**-ku save panna send pannum.
4. Storage server oru reference back kudukkum — andha file ippo enge irukku-nu.
5. Backend **metadata** (title, description, unnoda user id, and andha file reference)
   **database**-la oru new row ah save pannum.

## Step-by-step: video watch panradhu [#step-by-step-video-watch-panradhu]

1. Nee client-la oru video page open pannu.
2. Client **backend**-a andha video oda info kekkum.
3. Backend **database**-la irundhu row read pannum — title, description, view count, and
   stored file reference.
4. Backend andha data-a client ku back send pannum, actual video file enge irukku-nu
   including.
5. Client oda video player video bytes-a **storage server / CDN-la irundhu directly**
   fetch pannum — backend vazhiya route aagama — so playback fast ah irukkum, unnoda API
   server-a load pannadhu.

## Idhu future-ku enn mukkiyam [#idhu-future-ku-enn-mukkiyam]

Indha same split, nee build panra almost every real app-la varum: structured, searchable
data ku oru database, and files themselves ku (profile pictures, PDFs, audio, video) oru
storage service. Indha course-la, nee backend and database side-a FastAPI vechu thaniya
build pannuva; storage servers and CDNs usually oru cloud service than, nee scratch-la
irundhu build pannura thing illa.

Client, backend, database, and storage ellame place-la irukkumbodhu, oru real application
epadi build aagum-nu unakku ippo complete mental map irukku — idhirundhu ella something-um
backend piece-a properly build panna tools-a kathukura pathi than.

<Callout title="For you, coming from Express/Nest">
  Nee already therinja same architecture than — oru Express/Nest API structured data ku
  Postgres/MongoDB oda pesudhu, and files ku S3 (illa similar) oda, usually oru pre-signed
  upload URL illa oru multipart upload endpoint vazhi. FastAPI identical pattern-a follow
  pannum; nee inga puthu architecture kathukala, nee already munnadi build pannirukkura oru
  shape ku puthu syntax mattum than kathukura.
</Callout>


# Web 1.0, Web 2.0 & Why React (/tanglish/docs/fastapi/web-fundamentals/web-evolution-and-why-react)



Websites epozhume ippo work aagura maadhiri work aagala. React maadhiri tools ஏன்
exist pannudhu-nu puriya, avanga solve panna build aana problem-a nee paakanum.

## Web 1.0 — read-only pages [#web-10--read-only-pages]

Adhi earliest websites (roughly 1990s) **static and read-only** ah irundhuchu — oru app
vida, oru digital brochure-ku close ah. Oru server-la pre-written HTML files oda oru
folder irukkum, and every visitor ku exact ah same page than kidaikkum. Login illa,
comments illa, personalization illa. Nee just paapa, interact panna mudiyadhu.

## Web 2.0 — interactive web [#web-20--interactive-web]

2000s-la start aagi, web **interactive and user-driven** aachu: logins, comments, likes,
unnoda own content post panradhu — early Facebook, YouTube, comment sections vecha blogs
nenachiko. Server ippo every user ku *different* page generate pannum, database-la store
pannirukkura data vechu build panni.

Idhu oru huge leap forward — aana hood-ku kelaya, most Web 2.0 sites innum oru crucial
thing ku Web 1.0 maadhiri than work pannuchu: &#x2A;*every click entire page-a reload
pannuchu.**

## Full page reload problem [#full-page-reload-problem]

Oru traditional website-la (even oru modern-looking one, plain HTML/CSS/JS vechu build
pannirukku), oru link click pannu, idhu nadakkum:

<Mermaid
  chart="
graph TD
A[You click a link or submit a form] --> B[Browser throws away the entire current page]
B --> C[Browser sends a request for a brand new page]
C --> D[Server builds and sends a full HTML page]
D --> E[Browser reloads everything from scratch: HTML, CSS, JS, images]
E --> F[White flash, then the new page appears]
"
/>

Every single action — oru link click pannradhu, oru form submit pannradhu, oru post
like pannradhu kooda — meaning whole page-a throw away panni, zero-la irundhu rebuild
pannalam. Adhu solradhu:

* Old page disappear aagi, new one load aagumbodhu oru visible **white flash**
* **Ellame reset aagum** — scroll position, oru open dropdown, half-filled form, playing
  video — ellame pogum, en na browser completely start over pannudhu
* Nee already vechirukkura *same* CSS and JS files-a, every time re-download and re-run
  pannradhu

Oru chat app-a nenachiko, oru message send pannradhu entire page-a reload pannuchu,
unnoda scroll position wipe pannuchu, and whole app-a re-download pannuchu — just oru
new message kaatradhukku. Idhu ippo people expect pannura apps ku acceptable illa.

## React ஏன் [#react-ஏன்]

React (and similar tools) exist pannudhu exactly idha fix panna. Core idea: **page-a once
load pannu, appuram actual ah change aana chinna part mattum update pannu** — whole
thing-a epozhume throw away panni rebuild pannadhu.

<Mermaid
  chart="
graph TD
A[You click a button] --> B[JavaScript intercepts the click - no reload]
B --> C[JavaScript asks the server for just the data it needs]
C --> D[Server sends back data - not a full HTML page]
D --> E[React updates only the changed part of the page]
"
/>

Mேlе irukkura diagram-oda key difference notice pannu: server ippo full HTML page send
pannala — adhu **just data** than back send pannudhu. Indha course ku andha piece than
mostly mukkiyam.

## Backend developer ku idhu ஏன் mukkiyam [#backend-developer-ku-idhu-ஏன்-mukkiyam]

Indha shift, backend server oda velai enna-nu than change pannudhu:

|                               | Web 1.0 / 2.0 style    | Modern React-style             |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| Server back send pannuradhu   | Oru complete HTML page | Just data (usually JSON)       |
| Page-a yaar build pannuranga  | Server                 | Browser (React), once          |
| Every action-la enna nadakkum | Full page reload       | Change aana part mattum update |

**Idhu than exactly namma FastAPI kathukura reason**: Indha stack-la FastAPI oda velai,
HTML pages generate panradhu illa — adhu requests-ku data vechu answer pannuradhu than.
(Browser-la run aagura) Oru separate React app, andha data-a oru actual page-a maatti,
adha reload aagama update pannuradhukku responsible. Backend and frontend, requests and
responses of data vazhi mattum pesikkura rendu separate programs aagum.

<Callout title="For you, coming from Express/Nest">
  Nee almost certainly idha already pannirupa: EJS illa Pug maadhiri edhavadhu vechu oru
  template render panradhukku pathila `res.json({ ... })` call pannura oru Express route,
  *already* "modern" approach than — server oru pure data API ah, frontend oru separate
  React app ah. FastAPI andha exact same principle-la work pannum, so indha mental model
  unakku puthu illame illa — mattum adha sutthi irukkura Python syntax mattum puthu.
</Callout>


# What is a Database? (/tanglish/docs/fastapi/web-fundamentals/what-is-a-database)



Last lesson establish pannichu, backend oru trusted boundary-nu — client epavume secrets,
source code, illa raw data direct ah touch pannadhu. Aana backend ku andha data actual ah
**vekka** oru place venum. Adhukku than database irukku.

## Data-a oru variable-la store panna koodadha? [#data-a-oru-variable-la-store-panna-koodadha]

Nee nenachikalam, oru backend ellathayum plain Python list-la vechirukkum-nu, Python
Notes-la unnoda Final Practice exercise-la irundha `users` list maadhiri. Program run
aagumbodhu idhu velai seiyum — aana idhula oru fatal flaw irukku: &#x2A;*server restart aana
udane, ellame poidum.** Oru crash, oru deploy, oru simple reboot — ellame list-a
clean ah wipe pannidum.

Oru real application ku data:

* Restarts and crashes-a **survive** panna venum
* Millions of records irundha kooda fast ah **search and filter** aaganum
* Same time-la nadakkura pala requests-la safe ah **share** aaganum

Idhu oru dedicated software ku velai — oru **database**.

## Database-nu actual ah enna [#database-nu-actual-ah-enna]

Database solradhu oru separate program (usually adhoda own server ah run aagum), adhoda
whole purpose data-a reliable ah store panradhum, fast ah retrieve panradhum than. Idha
romba well-organized spreadsheets set-nu nenachiko:

* Oru **table** solradhu one spreadsheet — example ku, oru `users` table, illa oru
  `videos` table
* Oru **row** solradhu andha spreadsheet-la one record — one specific user, one specific
  video
* Oru **column** solradhu every row-kum irukkura one piece of information — `id`, `name`,
  `email`

```text
users table
┌────┬─────────┬───────────────────┐
│ id │ name    │ email             │
├────┼─────────┼───────────────────┤
│ 1  │ John    │ john@example.com  │
│ 2  │ David   │ david@example.com │
└────┴─────────┴───────────────────┘
```

Idhu unakku familiar ah irukanum — Python Notes-oda Phase 2 mattrum Final Practice-la nee
already work pannina list-of-dicts oda same shape than idhu. Oru database table
essentially andha same idea than, permanent ah and scale-la searchable ah pannirukku.

## Backend mattum than database oda pesum [#backend-mattum-than-database-oda-pesum]

<Mermaid
  chart="
graph LR
A[Client] -- request to a URL --> B[Backend]
B -- reads / writes data --> C[(Database)]
B -- only the resulting data --> A
"
/>

Client epavume database-ku direct ah connect aagadhu — database irukku-nu adhukku
theriyavume theriyathu. Adhu epozhume backend oda mattum than pesum, and backend than
enna read pannanum, enna write pannanum, enna back send pannanum-nu decide pannum. Idhu
last lesson-la irundha same trusted-boundary idea than, actual ah enna hide pannirukkom-nu
oru concrete example-oda.

## Indha course-la nee use pannura database type [#indha-course-la-nee-use-pannura-database-type]

Different families of databases irukku, aana most common kind — indha course FastAPI
oda use pannura kind — oru **relational database** (PostgreSQL illa MySQL maadhiri):
data clearly defined tables-la columns-oda organize pannirukkanum, mேlе irukkura `users`
table maadhiri. Idha properly hands-on ah future lesson-la paakuva — ippozhukku, just
indha mental picture-a vechiko: &#x2A;*tables, rows, columns, backend mattum reach panna
mudiyura oru server kulla irukku.**

<Callout title="For you, coming from Express/Nest">
  Exactly same relationship than `pg`, Prisma, illa TypeORM, oru Express/Nest server
  irundhu oru Postgres/MySQL database oda pesuradhu — client epozhume unnoda API-a mattum
  than call pannum, database-a never. FastAPI idhukku adhoda own tools use pannum (soon
  avatha nee paapa), aana architecture nee already pannikkittu irukkurathu oda identical
  than.
</Callout>


# What is a Website? (/tanglish/docs/fastapi/web-fundamentals/what-is-a-website)



Last lesson-la nee paatha, oru **server**, oru **client**-oda requests ku answer pannum-nu.
Oru website solradhu, most servers avanga answer ah back send pannura thing than.

## Moonu building blocks [#moonu-building-blocks]

Ethana complex ah irundhalum, every website moonu things-la irundhu than build aagum:

* **HTML** — structure and content (text, images, buttons — page-la enna irukku)
* **CSS** — styling (colors, spacing, fonts — idhu epadi kaanum)
* **JavaScript** — behavior (nee click pannumbodhu, type pannumbodhu, scroll pannumbodhu
  enna nadakkum)

Server oda velai, indha files-a edha browser kekkudho, adha send panradhu. Browser oda
velai, avatha read panni, nee actual ah paakkura page ah convert panradhu.

## Oru page visit pannumbodhu enna nadakkum [#oru-page-visit-pannumbodhu-enna-nadakkum]

Oru single webpage open panradhu rarely-a just *one* request — usually adhu one after
another, several requests ah irukkum:

<Mermaid
  chart="
graph TD
A[Browser requests index.html] --> B[Server sends the HTML file]
B --> C[Browser reads the HTML]
C --> D[Browser sees a link to style.css and requests it]
C --> E[Browser sees a link to script.js and requests it]
D --> F[Page is styled and interactive]
E --> F
"
/>

1. Browser page itself (`index.html`) kku kekkum.
2. Andha HTML read pannumbodhu, browser adhula oru stylesheet mattrum oru script file
   reference pannirukku-nu notice pannum.
3. Adhukku kooda **separate requests** send pannum.
4. Ellam vandha apparam, browser avatha ella combine panni, screen-la nee paakkura page ah
   pannum.

Idhu aprom mukkiyam aagum: diagram-la irukkura andha ovvoru arrow-um internet mela oru full
round trip — oru request, appuram oru response. Andha number-a chinna ah vecha (and
unnecessary ah repeat pannama irundha), web indha vazhi evolve aana reasons-la oru periya
part, adhu than exactly next lesson-la paakuradhu.


# What is the Internet? (/tanglish/docs/fastapi/web-fundamentals/what-is-the-internet)



Backend code oru line kooda ezhuda munnadi, actual ah nee enna mela build panra-nu unakku
clear ah theriyanum. So romba basic-la start pannalam: &#x2A;*internet-nu enna?**

## Simple ah oru definition [#simple-ah-oru-definition]

Internet-nu, world-la irukkura computers ellam oru huge network ah connect aayirukkardhu,
avanga onnu vodu onnu information send panna mudiyum.

Adhu than actually. Unnoda phone, unnoda laptop, and Instagram illa Netflix maadhiri apps
run pannura servers ellame indha same giant network-la irukkura computers than — chila
information kekkum, chila answer pannum.

## Ovvoru computer ku oru address irukku [#ovvoru-computer-ku-oru-address-irukku]

Oru computer innoru computer ku data send panna, adhukku enge send pannanum-nu theriyanum.
Internet-la irukkura every device ku oru **IP address** irukku — adha unique ah identify
pannura oru set of numbers, oru house ku postal address venum, andha edhavadhu mail
deliver panna mudiyum, adha maadhiri than.

```text
192.168.1.1
```

Nee rarely-a oru IP address-a nee typed pannuva — adhukku than `google.com` maadhiri
domain names irukku, avanga just oru human-friendly label, hood-ku IP address ah
translate aagum. Aana underlying idea same than: &#x2A;*internet-la irukkura every computer-a
oru address-la find pannalam.**

## Rendu roles: kekkardhum, answer pannradhum [#rendu-roles-kekkardhum-answer-pannradhum]

Internet-la nadakkura almost ella something-um rendu roles-ku boil down aagum:

* **Client** — edhavadhu kekkuraan (oru browser, oru mobile app)
* **Server** — answer pannuraan (epavum on-la irukkura oru computer, questions ku wait
  panniyirukkum)

<Mermaid
  chart="
graph LR
A[Client<br/>your browser or app] -- 1. Request --> B((The Internet))
B -- forwards it to --> C[Server<br/>a computer that is always on]
C -- 2. Response --> B
B -- delivers it back --> A
"
/>

Example ku, nee oru browser open panni oru website ku poga:

1. Unnoda browser (**client**) internet-ku oru **request** send pannum: "Indha webpage-a
   please kudunga."
2. Andha request network mela, adhoda address padi, correct computer ku travel pannum.
3. Andha computer (**server**) oru **response** back-la send pannum: actual webpage
   content.
4. Unnoda browser idha receive panni unnoda screen-la display pannum.

Indha request → response pattern than indha entire course-la mukkiyamana single idea.
Nee build panra ella something-um idhoda mela than run aagum.

## Idhu unakku enn mukkiyam [#idhu-unakku-enn-mukkiyam]

**Backend development-nu solradhu, indha picture-la "server" side build panradhu than** —
oru program, epavum on-la irukkum, requests ku wait pannikittu irukkum, and enna back
send pannanum-nu decide pannum.

Nee Python-la ippo varaikkum kathukitta ella something-um — functions, dictionaries,
classes — indha server *kulla* run aagura logic-a maara pogudhu, unnoda users oda
browsers and apps anuppura requests ku answer pannuradhukku.


# What is the Backend, and Why Do We Need One? (/tanglish/docs/fastapi/web-fundamentals/why-we-need-a-backend)



Backend, client/server picture-la "server" side-nu unakku already theriyum. Idhu lesson,
*ஏன்* idhu exist aaganum-nu paakuradhu — enn oru website just HTML, CSS, and JavaScript-a
mattum vechu, ellame browser-la nadakkanumnu irukka koodadhu?

## Ella something-ayum explain pannura oru rule [#ella-something-ayum-explain-pannura-oru-rule]

**Nee browser-ku enna send pannuraiyo, adha user paakalam, change pannalam.**

Edhavadhu website open pannu, right-click pannu, "View Source" illa DevTools open pannu —
every line of HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, adhu straight ah readable ah irukku. Browser-ku
reach aagura edhuvum private ah irukkadhu. "Find panna kashtam" illa — genuinely,
completely visible, and editable, adha open pannura yaaravadhu.

Backend exist pannuradhukku reason, chila things user ku **epozhume** visible illa
editable ah irukka koodadhu:

* Prices, discounts, permissions, illa scores decide pannura actual logic
* Passwords, and avatha epadi check pannuranga-nu
* Payment providers, email services, illa vera paid APIs ku secret keys
* Database itself — everyone oda data actual ah enge irukku-nu

## Client ku paakka allow pannradhu enna [#client-ku-paakka-allow-pannradhu-enna]

Oru user rendu things than epozhume paakuran:

1. Adhu call pannina **URL** (e.g. `POST /orders`)
2. Response-la enna **data** vandhuchu-nu

Andha response produce panna run aana code avan/aval paakka mattaanga. Backend oda internal
logic — adhu request-a epadi validate pannuchu, edha database check pannuchu, endha
business rules apply pannuchu — andha URL-oda mele side-la completely invisible.

<Mermaid
  chart="
graph LR
subgraph Client [Client - fully visible to the user]
A[HTML / CSS / JS you sent]
B[Whatever data arrives back]
end
subgraph Backend [Backend - fully hidden from the user]
C[Your source code]
D[Database]
E[Secret keys]
F[Business rules: pricing, permissions, validation]
end
A -- request to a URL --> C
C --> D
C --> E
C --> F
C -- only the resulting data --> B
"
/>

Backend oda whole point idhu than: idhu oru boundary. Requests uள்ள poidum, responses
veliya varum, and adhukkula nadakkura ella something-um developer oda business than, user
oda illa.

## Backend edhuvume illa na enna aagum? [#backend-edhuvume-illa-na-enna-aagum]

Nenachiko, *mattum* HTML, CSS, and JavaScript browser-la run aagura vechu oru online
store build panna try panra — server illa, database illa, hide panna edhuvum illa.

**Prices and discounts trust panna mudiyadhu.** "Final price" user oda own browser-la run
aagura JavaScript vechu calculate pannuna, user DevTools open panni checkout ku munnadi
idha change pannikalam. Real price-a check pannura second, trusted opinion edhuvum illa —
browser *than* the only opinion, and user adha fully control pannuran.

**Logins secure ah irukka mudiyadhu.** Password check panradhu `if (password ===
"admin123")` maadhiri oru JavaScript line ah irundha, andha string page oda source
code-la right there, edhavadhu yaaravadhu read panna mudiyum. Worse, oru user, avan/aval
own browser-la run aagura code-a edit panni, check-a entirely skip pannalam.

**Data share panna illa safe ah vekka mudiyadhu.** Database illama, data browser-la than
irukka mudiyum (e.g. `localStorage`) — meaning, adhu *andha one device-la, andha one
browser-la* than exist pannum, vera yaarukkume invisible ah. Rendu users onnu vodu onnoda
posts paakave mudiyadhu. Unnoda phone-la irundhu unnoda own account check panna mudiyadhu.
Browser data clear pannu, ellame forever poidum.

**Secrets secret ah irukka mudiyadhu.** Oru paid third-party service (email, SMS,
payments) call panna oru secret API key venum. Andha key browser JavaScript-la irundha,
adhu every visitor ku ship aagum — edhavadhu yaaravadhu page-la irundhu adha extract
panni, unnoda cost-la avanga own maadhiri use pannikalam.

Idhu ellame oru small inconvenience illa — meaning &#x2A;*site-la edhuvume actual ah trust
panna mudiyadhu.** "Konjam code run pannura oru page"-a "rules actually hold aagura oru
system" ah maatradhu than oru backend.

## Takeaway [#takeaway]

Backend than unnoda entire application-la, mattum *nee*, developer, control pannura oru
single place. User adhoda URLs call pannalam, adhoda responses paakkalam — aana adhoda
code, adhoda database, illa adhoda secrets epozhume illa. Idhirundhu FastAPI vechu nee
build panra ella something-um andha trusted boundary-kulla than irukkum.

<Callout title="For you, coming from Express/Nest">
  Idhu than exactly unnoda past projects-la kooda oru Express/Nest server enn irukku-nu — same
  "trusted boundary" idea than, request handler oru Express route-la, oru Nest controller
  method-la, illa — ippo start pannitu — oru FastAPI path operation function-la ezhudhinalum.
  Concept change aagadhu; syntax mattum than change aagum.
</Callout>
